abstract: With the development of intelligent substations, the problems of very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) and transient enclosure voltage (TEV) caused by gas insulated substation (GIS) disconnector operation become more prominent, which may not only cause harm to the insulation system of primary equipment, but also couple electromagnetic disturbance to secondary equipment. In this paper, TEV due to disconnector and circuit breaker operation were tested in a three-phase common box GIS substation. The VFTO and TEV co-simulation model is established in EMTP-ATP software. The VFTO and TEV waveform and spectrum are calculated and analyzed. Different arc models are used to simulate. The amplitude and frequency of VFTO and TEV waveform under different arc models are obtained. In this paper, KVVP2-22 cable commonly used in substations is selected to simulate the disturbance voltage of the secondary cable coupled by VFTO.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Voltage EMI Filter Using Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This work explores the integration of Virtual Reality (VR) technology into the design process of high-voltage Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) filters. The motivation lies in addressing the cumbersome and time-consuming nature of using 3D solvers for filter design. The research implements a VR environment allowing engineers to interact with a 3D model of an EMI filter, enabling dynamic manipulation of its geometry and electrical characteristics. By utilizing an emulation approach based on Kriging for the 3D solver and incorporating hand-tracking in VR, this work accelerates and streamlines the modeling process, offering an intuitive experience. The work demonstrates the significant potential of VR and Machine Learning in enhancing electrical component simulations. The successful incorporation of VR technology presents a pathway towards more intuitive and interactive EMI filter design. Empowering lab technicians and users alike, the presented approach simplifies filter design, allowing for intuitive experimentation akin to a hands-on lab environment.

articleTitle: Development of a Reference Source for Conducted Emission Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes an improved reference source that can produce Common Mode (CM) and Differential Mode (DM) separately. The reference source is used in conducted emission tests verification setup and Inter-laboratory Comparison (ILC) measurement. Conducted emission tests are important Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) tests that are performed by using Line Impedance Stabilization Network (LISN) and an EMI receiver in laboratories in accordance with emission standards such as MIL-STD-461G, RTCA/DO-160G, CISPR32 and CISPR 25. Each accredited EMC testing laboratory must carry out verifications using standard or own method to guarantee the accuracy and precision of test results. Moreover, the verification method reveals errors in the test setup beforehand and prevent incorrect testing in accordance with IEC17025. In this study, we introduce the design and production of the reference source, which meets the essential requirements of this standard. Finally, using the newly designed reference source, conducted emission test comparison measurements were carried out with the participation of three EMC laboratories within ASELSAN and the measurement results were presented.

articleTitle: Evaluation of On-the-fly Scanning Effects on Complex Field Retrieval Using a Single Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The on-the-fly (OTF) scanning method has become a popular technique for rapidly characterizing electromagnetic (EM) near-fields. A recent advancement in OTF methods enables high-resolution retrieval of complex fields using a single probe. This work investigates the scanning effects occurring in combination with this technique. Firstly, Faraday’s law of induction is employed to study the behavior of moving conductors in dynamic EM fields. Theoretical analysis reveals three distinct dependencies of the probe signal: frequency, probe movement, and the spatial distribution of the complex field. Subsequently, the scanning effects are numerically evaluated on a realistic microstrip line (MSL) structure exhibiting a dynamic field variation exceeding 70 dB. The results demonstrate that OTF scanning can achieve an accuracy surpassing 99.9% at any scanning speed below 10 m/s across the kHz to GHz range. In this regime, the primary source of OTF measurement error is the field magnitude distribution, which is largely independent of frequency. Finally, the MSL is measured at 100 MHz using a near-field scanner based on an industry robot with a maximum movement speed of 0.36 m/s. Compared to the OTF scanning effects, position tracing errors and signal acquisition accuracy have a more significant influence on the measurement. This highlights the efficiency and practical applicability of the single probe OTF scanning technique.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Information Leakage of Audio Signals Induced by RF Illumination
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Due to the wide use of voice communication across diverse IT equipment, the reception of audio compromising emanations (CE), introduces a vulnerability in terms of electromagnetic emission security (EMSEC). This paper demonstrates a method for the feasibility of electromagnetic (EM) leakage reception of audio signals by measurement of electrical changes in the information transmission process by RF illumination (irradiating EM waves) that cause information leakage. The effectiveness of the approach is evaluated through measurements conducted in an anechoic chamber. The method demonstrates that transmitted audio information, which cannot be detected by conventional TEMPEST test methods, can be obtained. In particular, when evaluating a voice communication device with headphones, we demonstrate that the output impedance of the integrated circuit (IC) undergoes changes corresponding to the output of the audio processing circuit, leading to amplitude modulation of the reflected waves. As a result, electromagnetic information leakage of audio signals induced by RF illumination could pose threats to a broader range of IT devices that use audio signals, necessitating the implementation of countermeasures.

articleTitle: Ionising Radiation Induced Changes in the Electromagnetic Emission of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this work, we explore changes in the electromagnetic emission (EME) of an integrated circuit (IC) induced by ionising radiation. For this, we use a custom IC consisting of several ring oscillator arrays fabricated in a TSMC 40 nm CMOS process. We utilise the 150-Ohm method according to IEC 61967-4 to measure the conducted electromagnetic emission of our test IC at one of the oscillator output pins. Between the EME measurements, we irradiate the IC with ionizing radiation produced by a high luminosity X-ray radiation source. Therefore we obtain EME spectra for the unirradiated IC and for doses up to 100 Mrad. In this paper we show the measurement results demonstrating an impact of ionising radiation on the conducted electromagnetic emission of our device under test (DUT). Contrary to previous assumptions, the frequency of the ring oscillators does not decrease steadily with increasing dose, but increases again between certain dose steps. We can justify our observations by taking into account transistor-level measurements which are provided by literature where an increased performance of NMOS devices at moderate doses compared to unirradiated devices is presented.

articleTitle: A Vector Fitting Procedure for the High-Frequency Model Generation of Inductive Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In order to simulate resonances in power electronic circuits and for EMC predictions, detailed high-frequency impedance models of the components must be used. Models with a relationship to physical reality are particularly useful for deriving design optimizations. In this work, a generally usable procedure for the generation of models for inductive power electronic components from impedance measurements is shown. A passive equivalent circuit model is determined from a rational function approximation generated by vector fitting in several steps. The procedure is shown for the secondary coil of a high-voltage transformer used in a resonant converter.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of a Non-Invasive Shielding Effectiveness Measurement Method in Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A recently published paper has introduced a shielding effectiveness (SE) measurement principle for which it is not necessary to place an internal sensor in the enclosure under test (EUT). This high-frequency technique takes advantage of the fundamental properties of a reverberation chamber (RC) and relies on the accurate estimation of its composite Q-factor for different test configurations. The technique uses an absorbing material placed successively in the RC, outside and inside the EUT. For an empty RC and each of these two configurations, the corresponding Q-factor is estimated, using an appropriate number of realizations of the RC. These successive estimates are used to recover the SE of the EUT. In this paper, we demonstrate experimentally that increasing the number of identical EUTs improves the sensitivity of the measurement, as theoretically claimed in the aforementioned publication.

articleTitle: Aggregated EMI Prediction in 2-150 kHz using Black Box Model of Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This work investigates the effects of frequency dependent grid impedance on the aggregated emission from multiple converters in the 2-150 kHz frequency range. Field-measured grid impedances, as well as normative reference impedances used in the 2-150 kHz range, are considered. Indeed, a suitable model based on a black box modelling approach is proposed to predict emissions. Results show that the aggregated emission from multiple converters is significantly influenced by the grid-to-converter impedance ratio. Additionally, the reference impedances used to represent the grid in the 2-150 kHz range, such as IEC61000-4-7 and CISPR 16-1-2 artificial mains networks (AMNs), are found to overestimate the grid voltage and underestimate current compared to the actual grid impedance. Furthermore, with an increasing number of converters connected to the grid, only a fraction of the individual converter current propagates to the grid. This dependence is determined by the converter-to-grid impedance ratio, while the remaining current circulates among the converters.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Domain Analysis of D-dot Sensor Calibration Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Calibration of D-dot sensors is essential before an electric field measurement. It requires knowing the frequency-domain amplitude and phase sensitivity with the associated uncertainties. Currently, no well-defined method provides vector uncertainties. This paper proposes an approach to calculating vector uncertainties with a discussion of the most influential sources.

articleTitle: SDR-Based Shielding Effectiveness Measurement Technique Using Signals-of-Opportunity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements of shielded cabinets can pose significant challenges because the typical procedure usually involves removing electronic equipment from the cabinet and relocating it to an accredited laboratory for measurements, a process known to be costly and time consuming. This paper proposes a novel measurement technique that utilizes signals of opportunity and software-defined radio (SDR) receivers to quickly estimate SE in a cost- and time-efficient manner. Moreover, this method facilitates continuous monitoring of the shielded environment to detect electromagnetic leakage resulting from intended or unintended shielding deterioration. Utilizing small antennas and affordable SDR-based receivers, the method enables on-site and continuous measurement of SE, even within cabinets heavily filled with electronics. This technique is particularly useful for TEMPEST cabinets because they are filled with electronics and require continuous monitoring due to the sensitivity of what is protected. Furthermore, its applicability may be extended to various other structures, where maintaining shielding integrity is critical. The paper concludes with a comprehensive discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of this measurement method.

articleTitle: Effect of EMI Filter Improvement Techniques on Conducted Emissions in a 48-12 DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The current trend towards the increase of switching frequencies in modern power converters is aimed at achieving higher power densities. This poses a great challenge to comply with stringent EMC normative, especially in automotive and aeronautical industries. They are clearly antagonist requirements since filtering and shielding techniques are usually required to fulfill those standards, but generally to the detriment of power density. For this reason, this work checks and compares the effectiveness of some cost-effective EMI filter improvement techniques that may provide modest attenuation enhancement of conducted emissions with a negligible power density cost in a real-case scenario, where the noise source is a laboratory prototype of a DC-DC power converter.

articleTitle: Studying the impact of shielding cabinet dimensions on cavity resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: As electronic components become more densely packed on printed circuit boards (PCBs), the risk of electromagnetic interference (EMI) due to unintended coupling increases. To optimize the performance of integrated circuits (ICs) and ensure electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), the use of board-level shields (BLS) becomes essential in mitigating EMI in PCB designs. The shielding cabinet (also known as a shielding can) is the most common component used for BLS. By connecting to the PCB’s reference plane, it provides five of the six walls required to form a Faraday cage. Although it is an effective solution in terms of shielding effectiveness (SE), it can lead to undesired effects such as cavity resonance problems. This study investigates the impact of cabinet dimensions on the cavity resonance frequency using a Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation modeling that is corroborated through an experimental measurement technique.

articleTitle: Research on Modelling Method of Conducted EMI in the Electric Drive System on Motor-Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: As the main Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) source in electric vehicles, the high-voltage electric drive system is required to test according to CISPR 25. And the test shall be carried out on the specified motor-load condition. To analyse and suppress the EMI noise, a high-precision model is proposed in this work. First, common- and differential-mode EMI paths are investigated. Second, a SPICE based simulation model is established. Typical high-voltage EMI filter, shielding cables and connections, drive motor, IGBT module are modelled and verified separately. Motor-load simulation with pulse width modulation is also realized in Simulink. Third, the whole system simulation in combination with the component SPICE models and the motor-load model is verified from 9KHz to 108MHz. Moreover, based on the established system-model simulation, the high-voltage EMI filter is designed to suppress the typical noise peaks. It can be shown that the proposed modelling method, especially considering the real motor-load condition, can effectively predict the EMI noise level. And high-efficiency noise suppression solutions could be achieved from the proposed system simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Influence to Radiated Emission Measurement in Consideration of Connection Direction of Unbalanced Power Line Termination Device to Outlet in Test Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The impedance characteristics of the outlet that supplies power to the EUT at EMC test sites influence emissions from the power cable of the EUT, resulting in poor correlation of measurement results between test sites. To address this problem, a VHF-LISN (Very High Frequency Line Impedance Stabilization Network) is considered as a power line termination device for determining outlet impedance. Currently, two types of VHF-LISN are proposed: balanced termination and unbalanced termination. Round-robin tests (conducted to verify the respective effects of the proposed VHF-LISN) showed that emissions from the power cable varied depending on the connection direction of the power plug of a differential mode (DM) signal source to the unbalanced VHF-LISN. We created a simpler power line termination device and performed evaluation using a highly reproducible method. The evaluation proved that radiated emissions of the balanced power line termination device remained unchanged irrespective of the power plug connection direction in the case of either a common mode (CM) or differential mode (DM) signal source. However, radiated emissions of the unbalanced power line termination device changed with differential mode (DM) signal sources.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence of Scanning Angle Error on Microwave Imaging Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Microwave imaging has garnered significant attention for its applicability in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). The precision of scanning angles plays a critical role in determining imaging quality, thereby directly influencing the effect of microwave imaging applications. In this paper, we undertake a comprehensive analysis of the scanning angle error in microwave imaging. Subsequently, we define four evaluation parameters aimed at quantitatively assessing imaging quality. Through a rigorous series of simulations, we have further study on the impact of angle error on image quality. The simulation results indicate that the sensitivity of imaging quality to angle error is influenced by scanning parameters such as antenna beamwidth, scanning distance (the distance between antenna and imaging plane) and aperture size. The research presented in this paper offers guidance and assistance for parameter determination in microwave imaging systems. Furthermore, the analytical methodology proposed herein exhibits a degree of generality.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of Polarization Effects on Antenna Measurement Near Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with the polarization effect on the antenna measurement near structures. To demonstrate its effect, the reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) is characterized experimentally using a triangular microstrip antenna array with circular polarization capability, whereby the results are plotted together with the ones of linearly-polarized antenna for comparison. The characterization is performed in close proximity to steel cabinet, solid wall, and pyramidal absorber at the desirable resonant frequency of 3.5 GHz. Moreover, the separation between the antenna under test and the structures is adjusted step-by-step from 0 to 4λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The characterization results demonstrate that the circularly-polarized antenna can provide superior performance compared to the linearly-polarized antenna when the antenna has to be arranged in the vicinity of other structures.

articleTitle: Cause of the Common-Mode Noise Suppression Effect of Y-Capacitor in Isolated DC/DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of power electronics is becoming increasingly challenging to manage. This is due, on the one hand, to the advancements in power electronics technology such as the spread of resonant converters, and on the other hand to the tightening EMC requirements. One of the most commonly used EMC measures in power electronics, and in particular isolated DC/DC converters, is adding a primary-secondary Y-capacitor to reduce common-mode (CM) electromagnetic interference (EMI). To provide a deeper understanding on how the Y-capacitor achieves this, CM impedance measurements on an isolated half-bridge LLC resonant DC/DC converter are presented in this paper. From the results, the reason behind the EMI mitigation effect of Y-capacitor can be observed which gives a more precise explanation on the underlying noise suppression mechanism and opens up an optimization opportunity for the technique.

articleTitle: Importance of Interface Variables for Closed-Loop Circuit EMC Co-Simulation Using WR Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This article highlights the importance of interface variables (IVs) for closed-loop co-simulating power converter controllers and electrical circuits using waveform relaxation (WR). The method enhances co-simulation performance and stability by adjusting relaxation parameters in parallel with the behavioral source. Testing is conducted on a buck converter circuit with an input voltage ranging from 4 to 6 V and an output voltage of 3.3 V. Comparative analysis with conventional WR indicates a voltage difference of less than 1.8% between direct and measured values after 24 iterations and 38.25 s elapsed time. An assessment of the suitability of this method to evaluate the conducted electromagnetic immunity of the converter is also provided. These results highlight the proposed method’s ability to achieve faster and more accurate convergence compared to traditional WR methods.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Immunity Test Method of Vehicle ADAS functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Due to the wide application of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in the automotive industry, it is necessary to evaluate the potential threat of ADAS functions in the complex electromagnetic environment. However, considering the lack of test method according to ISO 11451-2 [1] development of a comprehensive electromagnetic immunity test platform for the vehicle ADAS functions is necessary. In this paper, an ADAS test method is proposed based on the vehicle-in-the-loop (VHIL) concept for the electromagnetic immunity evaluation. Virtual scenes are built to calibrate the camera sensor, the radar sensor and the sensor fusion. Typical ADAS functions like Lane Departure Warning (LDW) and Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) with signal- and multiple-target are successfully activated in an anechoic chamber. The results show that the proposed test method and platform is feasible and effective for the ADAS electromagnetic immunity test.

articleTitle: A kind of high-rEp and high pulse-repetition-rate ultra-wideband radiation system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Avalanche transistors are widely used in Marx circuits to generate high-voltage pulses with a high pulse-repetition-rate. Since their power capacity is limited, for high-power ultra-wideband radiation systems based on solid-state pulsers, it is necessary to synthesis multiple modules simultaneously to enhance the total power. In this paper, a kind of high-$r E_{p}$ and high pulse-repetition-rate ultra-wideband radiation system is designed and developed based on space synthesis method. The system has 12 radiation modules, while each module consists of a solid-state pulser and a $2 \times 2$ combined antenna. The $r E_{p}$ of the system is 25 kV measured at 12 m, and the maximum PRF of the system is 100 kHz. Its polarization direction could be adjusted by a built-in motor.

articleTitle: Analysis of common mode noise coupling channel Between Vehicle Assembly and Ground Assembly in electric vehicle Wireless Power Transfer (WPT)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In contrast to conventional wired charging applications, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems for electric vehicles consist of two primary components: the Ground Assembly (GA) and the Vehicle Assembly (VA). These components are not physically connected by cables. However, from an Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) perspective, the GA and VA exhibit not only a wireless power transfer link but also a wireless Common Mode (CM) noise coupling channel. This channel allows noise to propagate between the GA and VA, impacting their Conducted Emissions (CE) performance. In this paper, this wireless coupling channel responsible for common mode noise is analyzed and the behavior of this channel is simulated. This simulation model is validated by comparing simulation results with both actual measurements and an analytic approach. Additionally, the influence of mains cable length on CM noise, which is transmitted through the ground floor of an Absorber-Lined Shielded Enclosure (ALSE), is investigated.

articleTitle: Comparison of Electromagnetic Parameters of Nanocrystalline Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper proposes a method of comparing toroidal nanocrystalline cores of different manufacturers, which includes both measurements and mathematical calculations of parameters such as magnetic flux density, permeability, saturation current, inductance of one coil, and volume of the magnetic conductor. For validation, the calculations are compared with the manufacturer’s datasheet. This method allows not to limit only to the data presented in the datasheet for 10 kHz and 100 kHz, but to see how the parameters of the core change in the whole range from 20 Hz to 200 kHz. This method will allow the electromagnetic core to be matched to the most demanding specifications by providing a broader view of its range of action.

articleTitle: Direct Lightning of a Compact Overhead Distribution Line with Covered Conductors and Periodic Grounding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Covered conductors are adopted for medium and high voltage overhead lines to limit the line right-of-way and the occurrence of faults to ground caused by external agents. The insulating layer of the phase aerial cables allows to diminish maintenance pruning in rural or remote areas and increase the resilience of these compact lines with respect to extreme weather events. This paper assesses the modeling of the line and the analysis of the results related to direct lightning of the messenger wire, i.e., the upper bare conductor installed for mechanical support. Indeed, in case of direct lightning, the messenger wire may act as an unintentional shield wire. Travelling voltages due to direct lightning of a compact distribution line are calculated, while investigating also the insulation withstand capability.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Framework for the Analysis and Modelling of Transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This work focuses on harness applications in the actual challenge of electric / hybrid aircraft propulsion where a particular care should be taken to cable management. This paper relies on joint deterministic and stochastic frameworks to provide intermediate cable harness modelling either improving the accuracy from simple models, or taking into account uncertain parameters.

articleTitle: Precise High-Frequency Impedance Measurements of Cylindrical Battery Cells for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Characterization of cells is a key step in the design process of battery packs. Measurement-based models allow simulations of battery packs and electric vehicles in the early design stage reducing development time and cost. This paper demonstrates a method for measuring battery cell impedance with higher precision and wider bandwidth using vector network analyzer in the frequency range from 1 MHz to 680 MHz. A printed circuit board (PCB) adapter is developed to connect the battery cell to coaxial cables and allow for repeatable results. Inductance dependence on state of charge and inductance dependence on axial position of the probe are presented. Proposals for further improvements are given.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Capacitance and Inductance Matrices Prediction of Multiconductor Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning-based approach for estimating the per-unit-length capacitance and inductance matrices ([C], [L]) of a multi-conductor transmission line. These matrices, key-parameters (with per unit length resistance and conductance matrices [R] and [G]) in the transmission line theory, are derived from the geometrical and electrical description of the cross section of the harness. Conventional methods typically involve either analytical models for very few simple configurations or numerical simulations to solve governing equations, as the Laplace equation related to the p.u.l parameters. In contrast, this study utilizes deep learning models to directly estimate these parameters, particularly focusing on the capacitance and inductance matrices. The effectiveness of the proposed method is compared to conventional numerical analysis, and strategies for constructing an efficient neural network for LC matrices calculations are discussed.

articleTitle: New SIL Calculation Software as per CISPR 16-1-5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The validation process of the antenna calibration sites as per CISPR 16-1-5 first requires the production of theoretical Site Insertion Loss (SIL) values based on dimensions of dipole antennas employed, three-port balun S parameters, the condition of the ground floor, and the measurement geometry such as antenna heights, measurement distance and polarization. In this study, a software solution that can calculate theoretical SIL values as per CISPR 16-1-5 was developed. Then the theoretical SIL results of the proposed software and a wellknown software solution referenced in CISPR 16-1-5 were compared in a variety of SIL geometries. Ultimately, our new calculable dipole antennas were verified at close distance in our anechoic chamber by using theoretical SIL values produced by the proposed software solution.

articleTitle: Improvement Method Using Complex Baseband Signals Against False Detection Caused by Electromagnetic Noise in FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar with fast-chirp can identify multi-target. In this radar, the beat frequency for calculating distance is in the MHz bands. So, for this FMCW radar it is required an ADC (Analog to Digital converter) with several ten MHz sampling frequency. On the other hands, WPT (Wireless Power Transfer) system for electronics devices are used in the MHz band. When the leakage power of these devices is applied to the ADC as electromagnetic noise, the noise signal would cause a false detection. We proposed a novel method using complex baseband signals and the latter half data after range fast Fourier transform to improve false detection. The effectiveness of the proposed method was confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: Magnetic Cleanliness Management in Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: To manage the attitude and orbit of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) magnetometers (MGM) are typically used. These equipments provide a coarse azimuth position by data processing of the three measured orthogonal components of the Earth magnetic field. As a consequence of their design features the MGMs are sensitive to the DC magnetic fields which can be generated by the satellite on-board equipments (e.g. RF switches, batteries, Travelling Wave Tube Amplifiers, PCBs…). Therefore, to guarantee the performance of the Magnetometers, the spacecraft design must be optimized to avoid unintended magnetic fields at their location. In small satellites the on-board equipment accommodation is critical due to the limited cavity room, therefore low DC magnetic fields at the location of sensitive units is generally reached by means of complex solutions like the use of booms [1], [2] or through proper electrical current routing [3]. The aim of this paper is to describe an approach to define the optimal accommodation of magnetometers in LEO small satellites by means of specific analysis tools.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Mirror Image Method Using 3D Poisson Summation Approach for Solving Antenna Problems in a Stirred Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: 3D Poisson Summation Approach is proposed to accelerate the MoM-based mirror image method (MIM) solution to antenna problems in large closed cavities such as Reverberation Chambers including radiating wire antennas and stirrers. The developed approach is validated by comparison of the fields due to a wire antenna in a realistic RC with direct MoM. The benefit of the proposed approach compared to direct MoM is confirmed. Its application to antenna problems in a stirred RC is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Variations in Portable Measurements of Radio-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This study explored the variability in portable measurements of radio frequency electromagnetic fields, highlighting their importance in risk communication and understanding individual exposure. Measurements were conducted by two volunteers using the same type of devices, protocols, and routes within 1 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area that was measured previously. While there were moderate correlations between the volunteers’ results, factors such as device characteristics, device uncertainty, and the human body’s impact could affect the results. Despite this, approximately 8 -80th percentile of the measurements, except for FM/TV, were within $\pm 5 \mathrm{~dB}$. The 10-90 percentile of data (except for FM/TV) distributes from -2.19 4.36 dB to $5.75 \sim 7.00 \mathrm{~dB}$. These results indicate a certain level of reliability in comparing results from the same type of device.

articleTitle: Measurement System for Electromagnetic Environment in Medicine using SDR with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Managing the electromagnetic environment in medicine is important for establishing a good reception of wireless communications. However, introducing measurement devices of electromagnetic environment such as spectrum analyzers into clinical settings is challenging owing to their cost and the requirement for specialized skills. In this study, we propose a measurement system for monitoring the electromagnetic environment in medicine using software-defined radio (SDR) technology and machine learning (ML). We evaluated the receiver sensitivity of SDR devices and developed ML models to estimate the carrier-to-noise ratio of wireless medical telemetry services.

articleTitle: Simulation of RF de-sense in small form factor stacked die packages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the simulation flow for estimating the RF receiver SNR and desensitization (desense) due to electromagnetic interference (EMI) in small form factor packages with RF transceivers and digital interfaces. Signals from digital clocks, with fast edge rates, that propagate through bondwires, and package structures placed near the RF macro couple magnetically (mainly) onto the RF transceiver on-die coils and package structures and can cause desense of the RF receiver.

articleTitle: Simple Formula for the Calculation of Shielding Effectiveness of Finite Width Conductive Shields
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, a fast and simple analytical formulation for the calculation of the shielding effectiveness of finite width conductive shields at extremely low frequency is proposed. The magnetic field generated by a current loop is analysed considering a conductive shield of various widths and for different distances of the source from the shield and from the field point. The effect of the system parameters on the shielding effectiveness is investigated. A formula for the shielding effectiveness of finite width conductive shields at extremely low frequency is derived from the values of the magnetic field in absence of the shield and in presence of a shield of infinite extension.

articleTitle: Alternative Materials for TEMPEST Facility Architectural Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Shielding is a fundamental aspect of TEMPEST precautions, preventing the interception of classified information within a defined zone. While existing literature analyzes shielding materials and their effectiveness for various purposes, a noticeable gap exists in papers addressing materials specifically for TEMPEST facility shielding. This paper explores commercially available shielding materials as alternatives for TEMPEST facility architectural shielding. The shielding effectiveness (SE) comparison is given for shielding window film, shielding paint, wire-mesh, and shielding fabric. Conducted in an anechoic chamber frequency range of 10 MHz to 6 $\mathbf{G H z}$, the results demonstrate the utility of these materials in enhancing TEMPEST facility shielding, offering alternatives to traditional metal plates. This paper brings diverse perspectives on the implementation of shielding as a precaution, especially in TEMPEST-protected facilities.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Impedance of an Electric Motor and the Impact of Material and Geometry Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We compute the common-mode impedance of an electric motor with hairpin conductors. We use a 2D model of the cross-section of the electric motor, where the per-unit-length parameters are computed by the finite element method (FEM). These results are then used in a transmission line model aligned with the motor axis, which gives an approximate 3D model with favorable computational cost. Given this model, we study the impact on the common-mode impedance given uncertainties in the material and geometry description of the motor’s cross-section. The results are useful for the understanding of uncertainties associated with manufacturing, temperature, aging, et cetera and how such uncertainties influence the EMC behavior in electric propulsion systems that are ubiquitous in the electrification of the transportation system.

articleTitle: Comparison of Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) Issue between Differential and Common Modes in USB Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This study addresses the rising concern of radio frequency interference (RFI) issue in high-speed connectors, particularly focus on comparing the radiation noise generated from differential-mode (DM) signals and common-mode (CM) noise. While prior research has concentrated on CM noises and their suppression methods due to their strong radiation efficiency, DM noises, despite possessing weaker radiation efficiency, have received less attention in past research. However, it is worth noting that DM signals possess at least 20 dB higher energy than CM signals in digital systems. To compare the radiation caused by CM noise and DM signals, a 3D model with USB 3.0 high-speed connector system is constructed and validated through full-wave simulations and near-field measurements. The simulated results reveal that radiation caused by DM signals exhibit comparable significance to that caused by CM noises in digital systems. This finding underscores the importance of considering DM signals and CM noises in digital systems and provides new insights into mitigating interference in electronic devices.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Restoration Method of Encoded Data from Electromagnetic Leakage Focusing on Error Detection Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In electromagnetic (EM) information leakage, conventional studies have focused primarily on unencoded information, which can often be partially restored despite losses. On the other hand, when targeting encoded data, even if there are errors of just a few bits, these errors can spread during decoding, making it difficult to restore the original information using conventional methods. To overcome these limitations, we propose a method that employs error detection codes— commonly included in transmission protocols for identifying noise interference—during the information restoration phase. This approach enables the complete and error-free restoration of data from leaked EM waves, even when dealing with encoded transmissions. Experimental validation demonstrates the efficacy of our method in fully restoring information from EM waves leaked from a webcam transmitting encoded signals.

articleTitle: Rogowski Coil Sensors with Optical Output for Lightning Current Measurement in Aircraft Fuselage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Rogowski coil sensor have been proven to be valuable for measuring transient currents. Some applications are focused on studying the current flow through metallic joints in airplane fuselages during lightning strikes. In this work, an improved Rogowski coil sensor with optical transmission is presented. Additionally, we report the results of current measurements across fasteners at the junction of two panels, considering different configurations with missing fasteners.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Shielding Effectiveness of Physically Small Enclosures Using Different Types of Receiving Antennas via Full-wave Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Shielding effectiveness (SE) is a crucial but challenging parameter for assessing the performance of shielding enclosures, particularly when dealing with physically small enclosures. IEEE Std. 299.1 outlines a standardized multi-port method using a reverberation chamber (RC) to effectively evaluate SE for such enclosures. However, uncertainties arise when the efficiencies of the two receiving antennas are unknown. When characterizing the SE of very small enclosures, the use of a straight monopole antenna (as specified in IEEE Std. 299.1) may not be practical. To address the problem of the physical implementation of a straight monopole in very small enclosures, both L-shaped antennas and PCB antennas are employed. To obtain the SE of the enclosures under test (EUT) with these two types of antennas, full-wave simulations are used. To overcome the challenges of the multi-port method, a simple two-antenna method is proposed and validated in this paper. Compared to straight monopoles, the L-shaped and PCB antennas can offer practical alternatives for evaluating SE in real-world industrial scenarios. Additionally, the two-antenna approach eliminates the need to know the receiving antenna’s efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimization of a VIRC Stirring Process using Frequency and Time Domain Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The stirring process optimization is a complex process which requires to deal with a large number of parameters. This communication presents first an overview of relevant frequency and time-domain metrics recently proposed. These metrics are then applied to a “fully-stirred” VIRC (i.e. suspended from the ground) now equipped with a set of 5 motors pushing the canvas randomly. The presented results clearly show that the stirring process is of better quality when the number of motor grows.

articleTitle: Adaptive Notch Filter Based on Electrically Variable Components for EMC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The use of a notch filter has significant advantages in cases where EMI is expected at a certain frequency and EMC has to be achieved. Notch filters provide high attenuation for a narrow specific frequency band, so they are very application-specific. In the case where the emission behavior changes over time, the notch filter’s effectiveness may be reduced. The ability of the filter to adjust itself to changing operating conditions will, therefore, significantly increase its efficiency. Such an adaptive notch filter can be part of a complex system that operates under a principle similar to cognitive radio. This study presents the electrically variable capacitor and inductors that can be used for such a filter. The proposed elements are examined within the assembled notch filter prototype via conducted insertion loss measurements for standard load/source impedance.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Based CDM ESD Current Target to Overcome Bandwidth Limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Reducing charged device model (CDM) electrostatic discharge (ESD) target levels for advanced integrated circuits (ICs) and systems on chip (SoCs) enables cost-effective manufacturing. Notably fast rise times, as low as 20 ps, have been observed for CDM events below 250 V. Previous investigations have highlighted fast rise times as critical parameters for damage in CDM testing of devices. These rapid rise times result in spectral frequency content exceeding 17.5 GHz, surpassing the bandwidth of existing CDM current targets employing disk resistors. To overcome this bandwidth limitation, a CDM current target comprised of parallel-connected transmission lines has been developed. Full-wave simulation results confirm the design of an initial prototype. Time-domain measurements conducted in an experimental setup exhibit exemplary results, with potential for further enhancement through de-embedding techniques.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Simple Power Analysis Using Backscattering from Switching Regulators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Even cryptographic modules once deemed immune to electromagnetic analysis (EMA) attacks through passive measurements have been reported as potentially vulnerable to EMA through active measurements. These measurements exploit backscattering induced by intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI). In this paper, we conduct a fundamental investigation into the feasibility of EMA through active measurement. It focuses on the behaviour of the output circuit of a switching regulator (SWR) integrated circuit (IC) with the sensitivity of active measurement in the MHz band, where attenuation effects are notably minimal. We discovered that it is possible to restore the output status of the SWRIC through backscattering in the MHz band. Furthermore, we demonstrate successful attacks, achieving an accuracy of 4.3% in correctly estimating the secret keys of 1024-bit RSA encryption, employing simple power analysis (SPA) based on their outputs.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiating Structure Input Impedance in Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper focuses on the study of the input impedance of radiating structures placed in a reverberation chamber, comparing it to what measured in an anechoic environment. The following emitters are considered, because usually responsible for radiated emissions in equipment under test (EUT): common mode current in a cable, differential mode current flowing into a closed circuit, and radiation from apertures. The analysis is performed via experimental measurements, by using a reverberation chamber and an anechoic corner. Differences in terms of input impedance have been observed in the case of common mode emissions and radiation from aperture in the EUT enclosure. Minor differences have been detected for the differential mode radiation.

articleTitle: Surges Induced in Secondary Circuits Due to Very-Fast Transients in Primary Circuits: Experimental Study Using a Test Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In recent years, numerous digital devices have been implemented as control and protection relay circuits in substations. Prior research raised concerns regarding failures in secondary circuits due to switching-induced surges, which occur during the operation of a disconnector in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). These surges are characterized by very-fast transients (VFTs) and manifest as inner surges in the MHz range, resulting from multiple reflections within the GIS. To devise effective mitigation strategies, the characteristics of these surges need to be determined. Moreover, the effectiveness of the potential countermeasures should be assessed via measurements or numerical simulations. Unfortunately, there is a scarcity of data and studies that thoroughly examine these characteristics. In this study, the characteristics of VFT-induced surges are experimentally quantified using a test platform that simulates the primary/secondary circuits of a GIS substation. Furthermore, we evaluated the effectiveness of surge-reduction techniques such as surge-absorbing capacitors, which are typically applied against lightning-induced surges and ferrite cores designed to address higher frequency surges. The findings provide general insights into the nature of induced surges.

articleTitle: Extraction of Noise Source Impedance of an operating high-power converter with high-EMI noises by increasing SNR using an amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents analytical expressions for the two current-probe method using an amplifier to extract accurate noise source impedance of an operating power converter. To improve the signal quality of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>-paramter when applying the two-probe method to the power converter in switching operation, a power amplifier is required between the vector network analyzer (VNA) and injecting current probe. For accurate extraction of the noise source impedance of the power converter, however, the effects of the amplifier should be accurately considered in the two-probe measurement method. Therefore, analytic expressions to eliminate the characteristic of power amplifier have been derived in this paper. The proposed method utilizing the derived expressions have been applied to 11 kW on-board charger (OBC) to demonstrate the feasibility of two-probe method in an environment with high-EMI noise.

articleTitle: Primary Frequency Control for Wind Power Plant using Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: An integrated RES and Battery energy storage system will be introduced to improve dynamic and transient stability and transmission capacity. The aim is to develop a control strategy for optimal use of RES and BESS. The study also examined energy management, operation control methods, and application examples of battery energy storage systems. As a grid-level application for energy management systems, real-time integration of a battery energy storage system and RES in grid control centers has been achieved. Some study cases are presented in which RES and BESS have been tested. Application scenarios such as power grid frequency tuning and power flow optimization are presented. In addition, in the study integrating RES and BESS into the power system, certain features support the voltage in electrical networks. Integrating RES and BESS units with optimum power factors has been shown to reduce energy loss, increase voltage stability, and provide primary frequency control.

articleTitle: Detection of Instantaneous EMC Failures in Reverberation Chambers and VIRC using a Generic Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This article presents a study on the possibility to detect instantaneous failures, which occur immediately after exceeding a certain field level, in a parallelepipedic reverberation chamber and in a VIRC(Vibrating Intrasic Reverberation Chamber). These failures are detected using a generic equipment under test (EUT) developed in this study. This equipment allows studying the impact of the stirring techniques on failures detection on a fair basis. Measurements are conducted in the reverberation chamber with step-wise stirring (i.e. fixed positions of the mode stirrer) with continuous stirring (i.e. continuous movement of the mode stirrer) and in the VIRC with continuous stirring only. It is shown that continuous stirring better highlights EUT failures and in the meantime allows a clear reduction of the measurement time.

articleTitle: Practical Considerations for Converting a Shielded Enclosure into a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The aim of this paper is to provide useful knowhow for the EMC engineering community to accomplish a successful establishment of a reverberation chamber (RC). To this end, the effect of the presence of different types of foreign objects on the field uniformity (FU) of an RC converted from a shielded chamber (SC) was investigated by means of simulations and validated by measurements. Furthermore, additional practical remarks were given in the context of measurement setup construction.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis of hybrid sharing the upper 6 GHz band between 5G NR networks and Wi-Fi devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The study evaluates the possibility of the shared use of the 6425-7125 MHz frequency band between licensed and unlicensed systems namely by 5G and Wi-Fi technologies respectively. Using Monte-Carlo analysis, the study simulates work of the 5G network in the presence of Wi-Fi devices with different density rates. The results of the study are presented as 5G downlink and uplink throughput losses due to the interference from Wi-Fi devices. Based on the results, it is shown that hybrid sharing of the upper 6 GHz band is not feasible and should be avoided.

articleTitle: An International Round-Robin Test for Insertion Impedance of Current Probes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The insertion impedance of current probes could have a large influence on an EMC test result, but only limited information about this property is found in international standards and in scientific literature. An international round-robin test had been carried out to gain more experience about this property and its measurement. The proposed measurement method works well below 500 kHz but has problems above with capacitive coupling between probe and calibration fixture.

articleTitle: Field Strength Check Standard Probe Comparisons to Historical Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Boulder, CO, USA provides measurements of radio frequency field probes in a standard field. This service provides calibrations to industry and other government agencies, and performs inter-comparisons with other national metrology institutes. Check standard probes are periodically measured to maintain the consistency of the standard fields used for calibration. The NIST field strength calibration service was greyed-out from 2014 to 2021 for renovations. After the renovation, measurements of check standards were performed and compared with historical data. Here we demonstrate equivalence of generated fields at the NIST facility from 1996 to 2024 across the frequency range 900 MHz to 10 GHz from 6 three-axis check standard probes.

articleTitle: ESD-Event Level Detection for Real-Time Monitoring of ESD Events in Manufacturing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A new ESD-event level detector has been designed and fabricated in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. The experimental results showed that it can detect ESD events generated from different kinds of ESD sources, including CDM ESD tester and IEC ESD generator. The core size of the silicon chip is only $550 \times$ $305 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$ realized in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. In addition, it can be further used to form an ESD-event level detection system for monitoring the real-time ESD events in the manufacturing environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Near Field Radiation at LPDDR5 DRAM with Various Operation Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper investigates the primary source of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) radiation at the chip level, a crucial step toward developing a low EMI chip. The study first seeks to determine which mode of Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) radiates the most. An Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) with an Hz probe is utilized to measure the EMI in various DRAM modes. Results indicate that although the current level in Refresh mode is comparable to that of Write mode, its impact is minimal because the internal circuit operation of DRAM is below 50 MHz. The maximum EMI level was observed in write mode at the spectral line of the fundamental harmonics of Command and Address (CA) and Data (DQ) patterns, indicating a correlation with the peripheral circuit. Consequently, it was concluded that Read/Write mode is the predominant radiation mode and that the IO simultaneous switchings are primarily associated with chip-level EMI.

articleTitle: Recognition of block cipher algorithms based on radiated emission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The paper describes the emissions radiated from integrated circuits when the ICs perform block encryption operations The article briefly describes several of the most popular block ciphers. A measurement station for leakage emission testing was designed. System emission measurements were carried out during AES, DES, SM4 encryption. Measurement results are presented

articleTitle: Assessment of Different Scenarios on Input Impedance of a Thin Wire
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper assesses effects of distinct scenarios on the measurement of the input impedance of cables connecting two devices. The test setup comprises two vertical reference planes and a horizontal reference plane parallel to which a thin wire is placed. The wire is soldered to SMA connectors on both sides, and these connectors are attached to the vertical reference planes. The wire is also connected to a measurement device on one side and linked to DUTs on the other side. The DUTs represent three extreme cases: open, short, and load terminations. Other possible scenarios fall approximately between these extremes. For each DUT, a measurement is conducted, and a comparison is made. The results reveal that changes in the input impedance are not solely due to the wire; rather, terminations and the reference planes of the devices also significantly impact the behavior of the input impedance.

articleTitle: Exposure to 5G mmWaves of a Base Station Operator: Dosimetric Study of the Influence of Posture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this work, the electric field induced by plane wave exposure inside a human model is numerically investigated. The focus has been on workers exposed to electromagnetic fields at the frequency of 26 GHz, belonging to the FR2 band of 5G technology. The results were obtained adopting a human anatomical model, studying an exposure scenario corresponding to the reference levels for local occupational exposure. The analysis was conducted on a specific anatomical region, i.e., the wrist, in different positions of the arm. The results show how the induced electric field may depend on the posture of the exposed subject and their anatomical characteristics.

articleTitle: Application of a Framework for Finding the Performance of Sampling Strategies for Electric Field Measurements in a Simple Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The current Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) directives have mandated a risk-based approach to assessing and mitigating electromagnetic interference (EMI) risks. In this context, in-situ measurement of electromagnetic (EM) fields acquired a strong importance, offering a perspective of which risks can occur in the intended environment of use. This paper explores and evaluates various sampling strategies of the electric field for enhancing and giving advice on in situ measurements. Through a systematic analysis, the performance of different sampling strategies is tested across diverse scenarios characterized by different frequency bands and the number of sources. Results give some first insight on each of these strategies when they can be used and what are the drawbacks and advantages. This study will reflect on the importance of understanding the EM fields in situ and the future work that would be done for further improvement in this area.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effects of Time Constants on Short Pulse Testing in Electromagnetic Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We have performed pulsed tests on a reference test setup inside two different reverberation chambers. One chamber has a time constant $\tau=1.5 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ while the other has $\tau=0.13 \mu s$. Failure thresholds of error functions are then measured and compared for the different chambers. We find that the failure thresholds are on average lower inside the reverberation chamber with $\tau=0.13 \mu s$. The lower average failure thresholds are concluded to most likely be due to a faster rise time and longer time at steady-state amplitudes of the electric fields, both being an effect of the lower time constants.

articleTitle: A Differential-Mode and Common-Mode DC-Bias VNA Measurement Setup for Power 4-Port Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A measurement setup for 4-port power electronic components is presented. The setup allows for the devices under test (DUT) to be DC-biased up to 10 A. The usable frequency range of the setup is from 50 kHz to 1 GHz. The usable frequency range can be extended down to 9 kHz (in compliance with CISPR 16-2-1) by using suitable bias tees, with otherwise no changes to the measurement setup. Therefore this work serves as a proof-of-concept for the measurement setup. S-parameter measurements of a common mode choke (CMC) are presented. Measurements with the proposed setup are compared to a reference measurement without the bias tees. These measurement results show that the influence of the bias tees is negligible, as was intended. Furthermore measurement results of the CMC under DC bias conditions are presented. A possible conversion of the S-parameters to the series impedance of the CMC is also shown to illustrate the possible applications of this measurement method.

articleTitle: AI Driven Power Integrity Compliant Design of High-Speed PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Modern high-speed PCB design places strict power integrity requirements on power distribution networks. More recently, artificial intelligence-based approaches have been presented to handle the increasing design complexity. In this paper, we improve upon existing deep learning implementations for real-time impedance prediction using convolutional neural networks and for automatic selection and placement of decoupling capacitors using deep reinforcement learning. Our approach relaxes restrictions on the number of different capacitor types and placement locations in prior surrogate models for fast impedance prediction. Our reinforcement learning implementation considers the impedance requirements of multiple active components simultaneously.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Uncertainty Tensorial-Analysis-ofNetworks of EMI Filter with Lumped Component Parasitic Effect Variability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A multi-parameter uncertainty analysis (UA) of common-mode (CM) EMI filter is introduced. After brief theoretical description, based on the Kron method, the tensorial-analysis-of-networks (TAN) modelling of the lumped EMI filter is established. The TAN model is validated by simulation with commonly used simulation tool. The influence of each constituting component parameter on the cut-off frequency, the insertion loss and rejection are investigated in the standard EMC compliance test band $150 \mathrm{kHz}-30 \mathrm{MHz}$. The dominant parameters with $+/-5 \%$ relative variation with inputs are identified from parametric AC simulations. Then, further MonteCarlo (MC) UA with 1,000 trials is run. The multi-parameter UAs of the EMI filter proof-of-concept with TAN model are discussed by using the MC. It was found how sensitive is the filter with the multi-parameter LC-component inaccuracy.

articleTitle: Reduction of Common-Mode Radiation in Electrical Drive Systems with Multi-Level Topology Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In inverter-driven drive systems, common-mode currents occur and can lead to high field emissions in battery electric vehicles (BEV) and aircraft and cause failures in subsystems. Filters and multilevel inverter topologies can be used to counteract such effects. In this work, the power train is identified and characterized as a coupling path for common-mode disturbances and an analytical approach for the prediction of radiated common-mode emissions is presented. A multilevel inverter is compared to a conventional inverter topology with respect to conducted interferences in the real operating environment. Finally, the effects of different inverter topologies and their switching patterns on the radiated field are evaluated in practical tests in a common-mode test bench.

articleTitle: EMI Reduction for Enhancing Measurement Performance of EM Wave Absorber Using Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper discusses the electromagnetic interference (EMI) reduction for measurement performance of electromagnetic (EM) wave absorber using horn antennas. The measurement performs five configurations, namely measurement of cable loss which performs maximum received signal, measurement of dual horn for achieving maximum interference level, and measurement of device under test (DUT) which consists of three scenarios. The scenarios of DUT are utilizing EM wave absorber with the dimensions of $27.84 \mathrm{~cm} \times 27.84$ cm, metal plate with the same dimensions of $27.84 \mathrm{~cm} \times 27.84$ cm, and commercial absorbent material. From the results, the EM wave absorber which was made of split ring resonator (SRR) with thin wire can reduce interference of EM wave at the frequency range of X-band (8 GHz to 12 GHz) with narrow frequency response compared to the one of commercial absorbent material. The decrement of power received by the EM wave absorber as the indicator of interference reduction and measurement performance enhancement can achieve -20.75 dB at the measurement distance of 25 cm compared to the measurements of metal plat.

Author Keywords: split ring resonator with thin wire

articleTitle: Investigating the EMI Shielding Effectiveness of Sustainable Biochar-Based Composites for 5G and 6G Mid-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Biochar and biochar-based materials find multiple uses in environmental applications that are expanding nowadays in the field of electronics and electrical engineering. With the rapid growth of technology in everyday, various electronic devices and systems emit electromagnetic waves causing interferences. For example, new vehicles have an increasing number of electronic systems which in return expands the requirements for EMI shielding solutions to minimize the emitted fields that could affect circuits in the vehicle. Thus, studying EMC and especially the critical field of proper EMI shielding to avoid interference problems is more than ever imperative. In this study, biochar-based materials with high electromagnetic shielding effectiveness are introduced as new and emerging use cases in modern telecommunications systems. Biochar was extracted from the pruning of the olive tree and was next mixed with carbon black, and the polytetrafluoroethylene as binder. Test samples have been characterized regarding their EMI shielding efficiency in the frequency range of 1-18 GHz, covering the spectrum applications in the 5 G and 6 G Mid-Band according to ASTM D4935-18 standard methodology. Results revealed that the proposed biochar presents shielding capabilities that reach almost 46 dB, especially in higher frequencies of the experiment. Our methodology demonstrated the feasibility of using biochar as a substrate to create composites with high shielding efficiency and evaluate the performance using a fast and easy-to-use laboratory approach.

articleTitle: Robustness Assessment of a High Performance, High Robustness IoT Processor Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electronic systems have to comply to electrical robustness requirements defined for their field of application. A TLP based stress test of varying rise time and pulse width is applied to UBS 3, Display Port and CAN Bus IO Interfaces. For a highly complex processor platform, a highly automated setup was implemented. It allows injection of pulses and the detection of hard and soft fails. Software based error detection, leakage measurements and current consumption were used to identify failure thresholds. The extracted failure threshold and high current IV behavior provide the basis for on-board design optimization for improved robustness following the SEED approach. The main novelty is the creation of a test method that allows to test three different I/Os using a common test principle.

articleTitle: Depth of Investigation in Measurements of Frequency-Dependent Soil Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The use of depth of investigation concept in measurements of frequency-dependent soil properties is examined. It was shown that the median value of the depth of investigation characteristic curve is more practically useful for arrays with perpendicular location of electrodes than the maximum value of the curve. At the same time, when soil is highly inhomogeneous and the measurement array dimensions differ significantly (for the same depth of investigation), there may be appreciable differences in apparent resistivities. In such a case, it is recommended to choose an appropriate electrode array, rather than just a certain depth of investigation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Prevention of Electromagnetic Leakage Scenarios in Automotive EMC Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The aim of this paper is to show the modeling of the possible ways of electromagnetic leakage in a shielding. The research collects scenarios of a wide frequency range, from a few kHz to the GHz domain; this includes the transparent wall, the outgoing surface currents, and the wave propagation through small gaps and apertures. Beside the modeling of the leakage path, a characteristic frequency range is assigned to each one, and the associated protections are also listed. This assignment becomes important when a limit violation appears in a radiated emission test because the measured result by itself does not carry any information about the path of the leakage. However, by discovering these, it is possible to infer the cause of the failure and perform a prevention against it. One of the leakage scenarios is thoroughly examined, the case of the outgoing surface currents originating from capacitive or inductive coupling, and it is demonstrated through FEM simulations, how to protect against this leakage. The tool of the protection is an RF-trap, which can decrease the electromagnetic field outside by reducing the leaking currents.

articleTitle: Noniterative Reference-Plane-Invariant Material Characterization Using CPW Line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic properties of materials can be determined through the measurement of s-parameters and the use of well-developed algorithms. For broad-band and accurate material characterization, transmission line methods are very attractive. While sample preparation can be challenging in coaxial and waveguide, planar transmission lines are well-suited to address this limitation. The positioning of the sample is crucial for obtaining accurate results in these techniques. We have applied a reference plane invariant technique, previously demonstrated only in coaxial and waveguide transmission lines, to a coplanar waveguide line for the first time, to the best of our knowledge. This approach eliminates the need for precise measurement of the sample’s position along the line. Flexibility and repeatability of the method has been shown using experimental and simulation results.

articleTitle: Analyzing Electromagnetic Interference Effects in Wireless Healthcare Equipment and Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This study explores the effects of electromagnetic emitters and operational environments on healthcare equipment, specifically electrocardiogram signal transmission over wireless local area networks as an example. Numerical simulations were performed to analyze interference scenarios in both open and enclosed environments. Performance parameters including amplitude probability distribution, kurtosis, skewness, and standard deviation were calculated according to the individual characteristics of both communication networks and electrocardiogram signals. Our simulation results show the impact electromagnetic disturbances produced on signal characteristics leading to distortion and information loss. As EMI levels increased we found variability in the signal characteristics including wider kurtosis, narrower skewness, and along with wider standard deviation ranges. These metrics are useful for understanding the electromagnetic environment and its relationships with the performance of communication systems in the presence of interference.

articleTitle: VNA-Based Total Radiated Power Measurements in Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for total radiated power (TRP) measurements in reverberation chambers, utilizing the capabilities of a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) without the need for a spectrum analyzer and signal generator. In contrast to conventional methods, this VNA-based approach offers a fast, simplified and efficient alternative for TRP testing in uncalibrated electromagnetic reverberation chambers (RCs).

articleTitle: Modeling the ESD Dynamic Behavior of TVS Based on a Time-dependent Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The traditional SPICE diode model does not fully characterize the response of transient voltage suppressor (TVS) under transient electrostatic discharge (ESD) pulses. This paper introduces a dynamic behavior model of the TVS diode under transient voltage, based on a time-dependent resistance model. Drawing on the similarity assumption that the avalanche breakdown behavior between the diode and the gas spark-gap device share physical mechanisms, the time-dependent arc resistance model of gas breakdown is utilized to describe the transient response behavior of TVS devices. Additionally, an extra series resistance is adopted to modify the arc resistance model, ensuring it matches the transient response curve. Consequently, consistency between simulation and measurement is achieved under transmission line pulse (TLP) pulses of varying voltage levels, verifying the accuracy of the model under ESD generator excitation.

articleTitle: Passive and Active Cancellation Loops for Magnetic Field Mitigation in SAE J2954 WPT Systems
