publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems are an attractive solution for recharging the battery of electric vehicles (EVs) because they improve safety and comfort. However, these systems generate high level magnetic fields that may interfere with nearby electronic devices and pose safety concerns for exposed people. In this research, the two most popular methods for mitigating the magnetic field in automotive WPT systems are compared: passive cancellation loops and active cancellation loops. The performance and practical factors of each technique are evaluated through theoretical analysis and simulations. The results numerically obtained provide insights into the effectiveness and suitability of these approaches in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of noise measurements at the HF band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The background noise is an important factor for radio systems using the high frequency (HF) band, since performance is often limited by the surrounding noise. ITU has published a recommendation describing sources of radio noise and noise levels for man-made noise in different environments. The recommendation is based on old measurements and more recent measurements have been made, with varying conclusions regarding the validity of the levels for different environments. In this paper, broadband measurements of the HF band were analysed. The measurement campaign consisted of measurements conducted over 36 days during winter conditions with measurements every 13 seconds of the whole HF band. The results showed a large variation of calculated hourly median noise figures in frequency as well as time, for the measurement period. For two specific frequencies, hourly and daily variations were investigated showing that large diurnal variations appear for lower frequencies. In this investigation it was evident that the actual time and length of the measurements on which the median noise figure is based are crucial. The results showed levels of the hourly median noise figure for the remote site between ITU Quiet rural and ITU Rural.

articleTitle: Utilizing Frequency Folding in Multichannel Measurements for Broadband EMI Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Due to the global electrification efforts, the electromagnetic environment has become increasingly complex. Therefore new, more advanced electromagnetic interference measurement methods are being developed, where multichannel measurement techniques have gained attention in recent years. This paper describes the utilization of frequency folding in oscilloscopes that do not have an anti-aliasing filter. To exploit this mixing effect, a filter structure is proposed where each filter has a bandwidth which is a multiple of the Nyquist frequency, extending the frequency range of the low-end oscilloscope. The filter structure was tested using a multi-tone test signal. It was possible to reconstruct the frequency components outside the original bandwidth and therefore effectively, tripling the measurement frequency range by simultaneously measuring the first three Nyquist zones.

articleTitle: EMI Risk Management: Leveraging EMC Assurance Cases and the Goal Structuring Notation for Effective Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Over the past few decades, there has been a noticeable increase in electromagnetic interference issues. Historically, assurance cases have been used effectively to demonstrate risk reduction, hazard mitigation and compliance to, e.g., safety requirements. However, despite the critical role of electromagnetic shielding in protecting sensitive electronic devices, no such assurance case has been put forth in this specific domain. Therefore, in this paper, we delve into electromagnetic compatibility assurance cases based on the goal structuring notation, with a specific focus on assuring effective shielding at both the component and enclosure levels. The primary objective is to present a compelling argument for why and how the system achieves sufficient shielding to mitigate identified electromagnetic interference risks in harsh electromagnetic environments. The proposed assurance case pattern establishes the necessary confidence in the applied shielding techniques throughout the system’s life cycle. By emphasizing the effective implementation of electromagnetic compatibility risk management strategies and the utilization of best practices in shielding design, this assurance pattern contributes to robust and reliable system performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Interconnects Routed Under PMC Based Heat Sinks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Perfect Magnetic Conductor (PMC) surfaces typically used for inhibiting resonances in metal enclosure are demonstrated to be effective also for limiting the unintentional EM radiation guided by the IC heat sink and the PCB ground plane. This PMC surface is realized by appropriately placing array of conductive pins under the heat sink and around the IC. Microstrip interconnects routed from/toward the IC are numerically analyzed to verify the impact of the close conductive pins on single-ended and differential traces; the crosstalk is analyzed as well to provide comprehensive guidelines for microstrip routing when a pinned heat sink is employed. If the layout is appropriately designed, the signal transmission and the crosstalk of microstrip interconnects are the same as the reference case of a heat sink without pins

articleTitle: Controlling HET Radiated Emission on a UHF communication payload in satellite scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The growing adoption of Hall Effect Thruster (HET) for Satellite propulsion system necessitate careful consideration of their impact on on-board communication Payloads performance. This is since the thrust is produced by the ionization of gas and accelerations of these ionized particles through and intensive E-field, with these complex processes generating electromagnetic radiation in a large frequency range, including the UHF Band.This paper shows the approaches followed by TAS-I to control this kind of interference for Narrow-band Communication Satellite (SATCOM) operating in UHF band. An alternative method is reported, based on modeling of a HET noise replica exploiting time domain measurements, then used in an End-toEnd system performance test. The reported activity drives the optimization of the accommodation of the HET with respect to UHF antenna to improve the decoupling of the HET killer from the receiver victim.

articleTitle: Rydberg Atom Electrometry: Recent Sensitivity and Bandwidth Improvements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We present recent improvements within the growing field of Rydberg atom sensors. Originally conceived as an absolute measurement of electric field, the research landscape has since evolved into the realm of quantum sensors and receivers. We discuss the capabilities and limitations of Rydberg atom receivers, and demonstrate how different atomic properties enhance or limit sensitivity and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Protection distances between HF-communication systems and wireless charging of vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Wireless charging of electrical vehicles use induction for the energy transfer between the charger and vehicle. It does not require direct contact as conductive charging does. A drawback of wireless charging is the radiated emissions that affects radio communication systems in the vicinity. This paper presents protection distances between systems for wireless charging of vehicles and radio receivers in the high frequency (HF) band. The protection distances are based on measurements of radiated emissions from a wireless charging station. Since the calculated protection distances show a large variation, a statistical description of the distances is also presented. It is not straightforward to give a general recommendation for protection distances in the HF band and for security reasons it can be argued that the maximum distances should be used. However, this might be unnecessary strict and an alternative way is to include the protection distances in a risk analysis.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Methods for Elaborating the Feasible Region for Signal Integrity Analysis in Differential Pair PCB Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: High-speed printed circuit board (PCB) design has recently evolved more and more towards differential signaling, as this has certain advantages over single-ended signal transmission in terms of noise immunity, crosstalk susceptibility and ground isolation. Even though all of these enhancements contribute to a robust signal integrity (SI), differential signal transmission raises further questions and problems especially regarding skew and timing margins. This requires to carefully route the signals symmetrically often resulting in a complex and time-consuming task for the PCB designer. Under these conditions, machine learning (ML) methods have shown to be effective for prediction of the relevant SI performance metrics and can thereby assist and simplify the PCB design process. In this paper, neural network (NN) regression methods are utilized to predict the signal behavior in form of measurements of the resulting eye diagrams, skew and timing margins, common-mode voltages as well as differential time domain reflectometry (TDR) responses from the given design parameters. Based on the trained NN models a genetic algorithm (GA) is utilized for optimization especially with respect to the feasible region of the electrical parameters, i.e. the design constraints that satisfy the specified thresholds for eye-width, eye-height, intra-pair skew and common-mode voltage.

articleTitle: Heaters Magnetic Emissions Control on Navigation Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Magnetic cleanliness is becoming more demanding for future Precise Satellite Navigation Systems (GALILEO, Moonlight) due the presence of atomic clocks sensitive to magnetic fields, in the range $\mathrm{DC}-\mathrm{mHz}$. Nevertheless, the presence of heaters in the nearby of clocks is also not avoidable since their performance are also dependant to very stable temperature variations (${\lt}3 \mathrm{E}-14 /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$). This will lead then during the TCS (Thermal Control Subsystem) design from the EMC engineer, to have tight control of the magnetic emissions from the heaters, especially where self-compensated ones cannot be used (i.e. for size or thermal reasons). This paper will give an analysis approach to lead the EMC engineer to prevent any magnetic interference in the early TCS design phase in the frame of satellites embarking atomic clocks.

articleTitle: Effect Analysis of the Ranging Function of FMCW Radar Excited by Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: When the frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is illuminated by electromagnetic interference, the interference signal is generated through the antenna coupling. The combination of the interference signal and the echo signal might result in errors in the ranging function. In this article, the effect analysis of the ranging function of FMCW radar excited by electromagnetic interference is carried out. The analysis consists of three parts. Firstly, the simulation is able to calculate the interference signal that enters the FMCW radar. Secondly, the analysis is able to derive the time-frequency plot of the interference signal after mixing, based on the principle of ranging. And it can be analyzed that the interference signal would be filtered by the low pass filter after mixing and would not affect the ranging function. Thirdly, the effect test can simulate the real situation of the radar excited by electromagnetic interference. The test results verify the effect analysis.

articleTitle: Summary of studies on ESD-induced conducted immunity test methods for spacecraft equipment and implementation into the EMC test requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) is one of the causes of functional failure of orbiting spacecraft. When electrical discharges occur, not only electromagnetic noise reaches the electrical units as radiated electromagnetic fields, but also the current generated by the discharge propagates through the spacecraft structure and becomes conducted noise, reaching the electronic units via spacecraft system harness. These noises are known to cause abnormal behaviour or permanent damage to electrical units. We have been studying the use of general-purpose EMC test equipment to verify immunity to conducted types of ESD originated noise. This paper presents an evaluation of the effectiveness of a new test method and an overview of a series of studies on ESD noise.

articleTitle: Empirical Validation of Signal Predistortion for Nonlinear Distortion Mitigation in RF Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Amplifiers are essential components in EMC testing setups. However, it generates levels of distortions that can significantly impact the electromagnetic emissions and susceptibility characteristics of the device under test (DUT), potentially leading to erroneous conclusions and wrong interpretation of test results. In this paper, it is presented the experimental investigation of a signal predistortion method aimed at reducing the power of harmonics and eliminating intermodulation products. This approach is proposed for conducting EMC immunity testing using multi-tone signals. For the linearization with signal predistortion, it is considered a static nonlinear model with memory to define the inverse model of the RF amplifier. This model is based on the Volterra series, specifically named generalized memory polynomial (GMP).

articleTitle: Maximum Emission from Electrically Large Sources in EMI Measurements - Comparing Measurements and Theoretical Estimates
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Increasing frequencies in emission measurements also increase the influence of the measurement methods used for established test sites. This paper shows a comparison of the measured maximum electric field strength of an artificial equipment under test (EUT) in a fully anechoic room. The influence of the spatial scanning on the measured maximum electric field strength is presented. The estimate of the directivity based on the electrical size of the EUT will be shown. This is important to evaluate the validity of measurements and to understand the correlation and reasons for differences between measurements in established and alternative test sites. In order to reduce time-consuming measurements and increase test efficiency, statistical methods should be taken into account to estimate the maximum emission based on a technically and economically reasonable sampling of the EUT’s emission.

articleTitle: An EMC-Investigation on Dead Time Distortion of SiC Based Half Bridge LLC Resonant Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: To guarantee the safe operation of switching devices and accomplish zero voltage switching (ZVS), it is crucial to determine the dead time in a half-bridge LLC resonant inverter. When the resonant inverter fails to meet the ZVS boundary, the voltage reversal occurs across the switching devices with high voltage/current transitions leading to the distortion event. This work provides the opportunity to investigate the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) issues of the half bridge LLC resonant inverter in the context of varying dead time. Hardware results from an experimental setup demonstrate the impact of dead time distortion on the switching device and their correlation with EMC challenges, which are validated by measurements performed in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: A Physics-driven and Data-driven Digital Twin for Vehicle Immunity Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We present a digital twin approach for the systematic evaluation and prediction of critical configurations in vehicle immunity testing. Based on parameterized simulation models, training and test data for regression and classification models (supervised learning) are generated. White box machine learning models are used so that the user can interpret and explain the results and relationships between the attributes and responses. This makes it possible to predict at an early vehicle development phase which components could prove critical during final vehicle testing. It is shown how to use this approach to evaluate in which vehicle variant a component will be exposed to worst-case conditions.

articleTitle: Analyzing Bit Error Propagation in Multilayer Communication Networks: Codebook Method to Combine TMR and Hamming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper explores the integration of error detection and correction mechanisms in a multilayer communication network to reveal the benefits of transmitting warnings about potential bit errors. We introduce a novel decoding technique for Hamming codes, termed the codebook method, which utilizes information from other layers to enhance decoding accuracy and minimize False Positive (FP). However, the effectiveness of this method relies upon the quality of the detector. Additionally, we investigate the potential of a hybrid approach by integrating the Hamming decoder with the codebook method, which shows promising results in reducing FP but may compromise performance in terms of False Negative (FN), particularly in safety-critical systems.

articleTitle: An Insight into the Practical Problems of Near-field to Far-field Transformation in the Time Domain for EMI Test
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Far-field prediction was achieved using time domain near-field on a rectangular Huygens surface. Both electric and magnetic fields are measured in the time domain and processed to predict far-field radiation. An example is used to verify the method and practical issues are addressed to guide the reader on how to perform a time domain near-field measurement. The predicted far-field results are validated by simulation and anechoic chamber measurements. It is shown at low frequencies, here 30 MHz, at which the DUT hardly radiates ($195 \times 150 \times 200 \mathrm{~cm}$ large), the transformation fails as the reactive near field is much stronger than the radiating components of the near field.

articleTitle: Extended Capabilities of PEEC-based Approach for the Modelling and Design of Common-Mode Chokes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents modelling methodology for common-mode chokes (CMC) with multi-wire (double or triplewire) winding’s structure, bifilar CMC and 4-phase power inductors with toroidal and oval-shaped magnetic cores. Simulation models are based on the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method. Validation of the PEEC-based models of the examined chokes is performed by comparison of the calculated impedances with results of 3D modelling and measurements.

articleTitle: Multi-port Thévenin’s Theorem: A New Matrix Formulation and Efficient Calculation Method of Equivalent Circuit Constants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A new matrix formulation for the multi-port Théenin’s theorem is proposed, which allows each port to be represented by a single equivalent source, while specifying whether it is a voltage or current source. Additionally, an efficient method for determining the values of these equivalent sources using Tellegen’s theorem and inter-reciprocity is described. The method described in this paper is applied to the equivalent circuit analysis of a power supply circuit that provides multiple voltages or currents in an electronic device.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Microwave Absorbers Based on High-Impedance Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The simulation model and the optimal design methodology for absorbers consisting of metallic patches on a dielectric substrate backed by a perfectly conductive layer, have been developed. New expressions for the real and imaginary parts of the substrate permittivity are proposed to achieve a desired reflection coefficient at a specified resonance frequency. This analytical formulation is then utilized to predict the absorbance performance of various structures under both normal and oblique incidence plane waves up to 10 GHz. Validation of the obtained results is conducted by comparing them with those obtained from CST full-wave numerical simulations.

articleTitle: S-Parameters Characterization for EMI Filters: Limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the S-parameters measurement techniques for electromagnetic interference filter performance evaluation using single-ended to mixed-mode conversion and pure-mode approaches In conjunction with an SDR-based vector network analyzer, it investigates the feasibility and accuracy of these techniques. Experimental results from testing commercial off-the-shelf filters and custom-made notch filters are presented, demonstrating the capabilities and limitations of used measurement techniques, and highlighting the influence of VNA parameters on measurement accuracy and the trade-off between speed and precision of the measurement results.

articleTitle: Classification and Modelling of Power Line Communication Channel in the Narrowband Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Narrowband power line communication (PLC) adequately ensures consumption control, management of indoor electrical appliances as well as communication between electric vehicles and recharging sockets. However, electrical cables are not designed to ensure reliable data transmission. Several disturbance phenomena can have an impact on communication over power lines. Thus, evaluating the performance of this technology requires good knowledge of channel behavior. The main contribution of this study consists on conducting enhanced analysis on the performance of the indoor PLC channel in the 9 kHz–500 kHz band. Results of a channel response measurements campaign in which more than 10,000 measurements, realized in 13 sites, are used in this evaluation. The measured channels were classified according to their channel capacity into five classes and modelled using Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filters. The fitting algorithm and other modelling methods utilized are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Correlating Shielding Effectiveness and Wave Impedance for Characterizing Low-Frequency Board Level Shields using the Stripline Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper investigates the correlation between shielding effectiveness and wave impedance for the characterization of board-level shields from 10 MHz up to 10 GHz by simulation models. Full-wave simulations are performed using the Finite-Difference-Time-Domain solver. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between electric and magnetic sources when characterizing the practical performance of board-level shields for on-board shielding applications, especially considering the short distances between the shields and on-board sources. Additionally, the good level of agreement between the measured and simulated shielding effectiveness results is shown for both the $50 \Omega$ matched microstrip and the patch source. Notably, this clarification underscores that the microstrip does not function as a magnetic source, while the patch source indeed acts as an electric source when characterizing board-level shields.

articleTitle: Development of an In-Situ Detection Mechanism for Common-Mode Choke Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The saturation of the common mode chokes (CMCs) in the electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters can impair filter performance, increase EMI issues and reduce efficiency. Detecting saturation in operational conditions presents a significant challenge. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for detecting choke saturation using a three-winding configuration. One winding creates core saturation through the application of DC current, while another introduces high-frequency signals for detection by the third winding. The change in the detected signal indicates saturation. Experimental data validate the proposed detection mechanism, providing a complete understanding of its effectiveness in operating conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of High-Voltage Bias-Tee for Capacitor Characterization under DC Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The voltage dependence of capacitors is important for various applications such as EMC filters and DC link structures in power electronics, as it can significantly affect the device behavior. Understanding capacitance variation over wide bias ranges, including up to kilovolt levels, is of particular interest and has been the subject of numerous academic studies. As these academic studies use self-built bias structures (bias tees) for high voltage and/or high current DC biasing during impedance measurements, replicating such setups is often challenging. This study presents the application of a commercially available 1000V bias tee for capacitance extraction using a vector network analyzer. Necessary procedures, such as setup calibration, are described in detail and the accuracy of the approach is analyzed. A Ceralink ceramic capacitor is used as the device under test and a voltage-independent thin film capacitor as reference.

articleTitle: Computational RF Dosimetry of Rodents Cohorts in a Realistic Reverberation Chambers at 900 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Reverberation chambers (RCs) have been widely employed in bioelectromagnetic large-scale rodent bioassays, to investigate potential effects of lifetime RF exposures. Numerical RF dosimetry has been of the utmost importance in determining the range of exposures, in terms of whole-body and organ specific absorption rate (SAR), and its uniformity across large animal cohorts, and therefore may influence key decisions in the design of in-vivo animal studies (exposure levels, number of animals per room, etc.). In this work, we expand prior research on rodents’ numerical dosimetry in RCs based on a realistic RC configuration, comprising a mode stirrer and various types of antennas. The exposure prediction modeling involves a MonteCarlo (MC) approach recently developed by the authors, taking into account the animals size distribution, as well as their posture, position and orientation within individual cages. The feasibility of conducting whole-RC dosimetry within a multivariate MC framework for large rodent cohorts at 900 MHz was demonstrated, showing larger whole-body SAR (wbSAR) variability than previously estimated, and suggesting that exposures in some of the cages may be consistently higher or lower than a cohort mean wbSAR target.

articleTitle: Comparing the Four-Antenna and Two-Antenna Methods for Shielding Effectiveness Characterisation in a Double Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes a comparison between two methods to characterize the shielding effectiveness (SE) of materials in a double reverberation chamber (RC). The first method is the two-antenna approach, which measures coupling with and without material between the source and measurement antenna, to calculate SE. The second method is the four-antenna approach, which also considers chamber losses. The central question is whether the use of two additional antennas and a four-port vector network analyzer (VNA) is necessary for accurate SE characterization. The results show that there is no big difference between the two-antenna and four-antenna method.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Study of an Energy Storage Effect in Nonlinearly loaded Receiving Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Receiving antenna structures that include nonlinear loads may exhibit remarkable behavior if they are illuminated by electromagnetic waves. Former studies revealed that an energy storage effect can be observed if loads with strong nonlinear characteristics are included in an antenna structure. This particular effect is visible as an approximate DC-component included in the signal measured at the antenna’s feed. A special behavior occurs when such a receiving structure is subject to a short transient excitation. We can state that the approximate DC-component is measurable for a duration that largely exceeds the decay time of the oscillations caused by the transient interference. In this contribution, the effect will be analyzed using macromodeling techniques in order to compute currents and voltages at nonlinear loads with the aim to provide a deeper understanding regarding this energy storage effect. Finally it will be shown that besides the fact that such an energy storage property is a major issue regarding EMC, it may be exploited for the measurement of pulsed excitations.

articleTitle: A Miniature Resonant Magnetic Field Probe Integrated with MLCC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this work, a miniature resonant probe for detecting normal magnetic field, integrated with multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC), is introduced. The probe features an LC resonance structure, where metal loops serve as inductor (L) and MLCC functions as capacitor (C, resulting in enhanced sensitivity at the resonant frequency of 2.4 GHz. The probe is first modelled and simulated cooperated with S parameters of balun and MLCC, followed by fabrication and measurement utilizing a near-field scanning system. The consistency between the simulated and measured sensitivity validates the excellent performance of the probe. This innovative probe exhibits promising potential applications for capturing faint radiation emitted by WIFI antennas and accurately locating the sources of radiation.

articleTitle: Timing-Controlled EM Fault Injection Method Focusing on EM Leakage from Communication Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Fault injection attacks against cryptographic modules have been identified as a significant threat, as they can be used to extract secret keys by inducing temporary fault at a specific timing during cryptographic operations. Conventional fault injection methods typically involve fault triggering by exploiting signals that indicate the execution time of cryptographic operations or common-mode currents that are highly relevant to these operations and then injecting electromagnetic (EM) waves synchronized with these signals. However, inducing faults only for a specific process is challenging owing to delays between observing trigger signals and injecting EM waves. In addition, countermeasures against side-channel attacks may prevent sensitive information from leaking outside the cryptographic module, making conventional methods ineffective in certain scenarios. To address these challenges, this study proposes a fault injection method that leverages common-mode currents generated during the communication process as trigger signals to induce faults at arbitrary times during cryptographic operations. The method was validated on a device implemented with AES-128. The probability of fault injection at a particular process was approximately 50%. To further enhance precision, the transmission time of ciphertext from the cryptographic module was considered. Our proposed method can successfully generate the faults required to extract secret keys, ultimately allowing for the retrieval of these keys.

articleTitle: Study of the Multifrequency Susceptibility of Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with the susceptibility of operational amplifiers (op-amps) in multifrequency injection. After an in-depth analysis of the different failure mechanisms that induces DC-offset based on experimental results on a general-purpose op-amp, the paper proposes a risk assessment method based on continuous wave susceptibility test results.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Modelling & Evaluation of Filament-Loaded Concrete for Facilities Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Recent progress in Fiber Reinforced Concrete (FRC) are described, mainly the absorption and reflection shielding factors. RF power attenuation is a predictable function of loaded concrete thickness, type and size of fibers, combined with a metal mesh that complement the concrete for providing low frequency shielding. This solution, achieving more than 50 dB shielding across the whole $10 \mathrm{MHz}-10 \mathrm{GHz}$ span, is competing with the traditional method of erecting Faraday cages inside a building.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cable Factors on Shielding Effectiveness Measurements with GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this work, we focus on the shielding effectiveness (SE) of cables using a Gigahertz Transverse Electromagnetic (GTEM) cell which is an alternative measurement setup for radiation and emission measurements. Even if the GTEM cell imparts unique properties such as compactness, the need for less power to create fields, and no need for antennas, SE measurements of cables with it can lead to deviations and unrepeatable results. Thus, this paper focuses on the reasons by following a methodology that combines a statistical analysis of the measured SE while varying cable type, cable position, and cable terminations. This way we ensure the repeatability of our measurements and show the effects of these variants on the SE results.

articleTitle: Markov Decision Processes to Model Decision-making in Harsh Electromagnetic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) poses a significant threat to the safe and reliable operation of electronic devices. Implementing data triplication and EMI-detection techniques are effective approaches to improve electromagnetic resilience. Although detector warnings can prompt the system into a safe state, they may also decrease system availability and increase data uncertainty. Nonetheless, prioritising EM resilience is essential for organisations that rely heavily on electronic devices. This paper presents a Markov decision process-based approach to model decision-making in a reverberant electromagnetic environment. To determine the optimal action in each state, the model calculates the state transition probabilities using the warnings generated by the EMI detector. The effectiveness of the decision model is assessed by testing it against various frequencies of EMI and bit rates. The findings suggest a significant decrease of 24.8 0% in the symbol error rate, compared to the baseline scenario. These results demonstrate the value of implementing a decision model in order to reduce errors and improve performance.

articleTitle: Practical Considerations for the Use of Comb Generators in Shielding Effectiveness Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A comparison of commercial-of-the-shelf (COTS) reference radiators for in-situ shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements is presented in this study. Pitfalls in current SE standards are examined, and improvements based on including small-footprint and self-reliant transmitting reference radiators is presented. The deployment of reference radiators based on comb generators is shown to simplify the SE measurement procedure, especially in the case of in-situ measurements. However, their performance is not expected to be the same as in the case of conventional techniques utilizing a signal generator with a power amplifier. On the other hand, in-situ measurements are known to be bound to higher measurement uncertainties, therefore the imperfections of the source are not as critical as in laboratory conditions. Still, in the case of SE measurements, the dynamic range (DR) is always of high importance. In this paper, parameters affecting the DR including output power level and pulse repetition frequency (PRF) are addressed both experimentally and theoretically. A comparison between the typical output power data of common reference radiators is shown, discussed, and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Uniform magnetic field coils construction optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Optimization of uniform magnetic field generation through the variation of magnetic coil sizes and positions is derived through calculation of the magnetic field of ideal circular coils for Helmholtz and Maxwell coils, achieving at least 20% increase of uniform field area. Analytical solution for Biot-Savart law for circular current loop is used to perform all computational results. Sensitivity to dimensional imperfections is given and it is also shown that multi-turn coils have negligible effect on the generated field as long as coil cross-section dimensions are small compared to coil radius. The reference calculation results are compared by experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Broadband Circuit Model of Common Mode Chokes for EMI pre-compliance assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Common mode chokes (CMCs) are used inside electro-magnetic interference (EMI) filter to suppress unwanted noise. Together with filter capacitors, CMCs can provide low-pass (LP) RLC filtering behavior. Two-winding CMCs are characterized by a common mode impedance $Z_{C}$ that is the impedance seen by common mode noise, and by a differential mode impedance $Z_{D}$, which is dependent on the leakage inductance. Other impedances characterizing a CMC are the inter-winding impedance ($Z_{I W}$), which is the impedance seen at the two terminals of the CMC, and the phase impedance $\left(Z_{P H}\right)$, that is the impedance seen from an input to output of the same winding. All these impedances can be assessed by measurement at the Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), or by means of an impedance analyzer. In this work we show how to construct a broadband model of the CMC, suitable for EMI pre-compliance assessment, by merging all the information of the four measurements related to the two-winding CMCs. This model might help hardware/power electronics engineers to perform preliminary simulations of the insertion losses of EMI filter, and to know in advance the minimum required falling slope necessary to achieve electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) pre-compliance.

articleTitle: Separating Sections of a Research Facility to Minimize the Spread of EMI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Earthing in an industrial context is normally split into Protective Earthing and Protective Bonding for safety reasons and Functional Bonding where needed to prevent the spread of EMI. This paper investigates how a situation can be handled where it is not possible to fully use this approach in a large facility. Following the traditional pattern would mean introducing unwanted galvanic paths for possible spread of EMI. Therefore a new take on the earthing system is needed and safety has to be addressed in a novel fashion.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Detection of Counterfeit Parts with Abnormal Aging Characteristics Using Electromagnetic Backscattering from I/O Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Due to a global shortage of semiconductors, there are growing concerns about the long-term availability of legacy semiconductor chips. As a result, maintaining backstock products and using refurbished products are becoming practical maintenance strategies. In such situations, there’s a risk that “counterfeit parts” - counterfeit or imitation chips, or chips with abnormal aging characteristics - might enter the market. These counterfeit parts require technologies to identify and eliminate them. This article focuses on counterfeit parts with abnormal aging characteristics and proposes a method to detect non-invasively whether such integrated circuits (ICs) are present inside a device without opening it. The proposed method confirmed that by irradiating the device to electromagnetic waves of about 1065 MHz with an intensity of 30 dBm, ICs could be detected by accelerated testing in which an overvoltage was applied.

articleTitle: Origin of the Damped Oscillatory Waves in the MV Mains of the High Current Testing Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The High Current Testing Laboratory (HCTL) must be safe for the operational staff. Moreover, the equipment supervising the test must operate without any malfunctions. Relevant elements of the setup in the HCTLs are a three-phase 15 kV supply source, a medium voltage (MV) circuit breaker (CB), a three-phase supply line, a medium voltage/low voltage (MV/LV) transformer and a short circuit switch in the circuit at the secondary side of the transformer. The time-phase controller used for supervising the test in the HCTL under consideration is observed to get sporadically out of control by switching ON the MV CB. Unexpectedly, it starts the test immediately, i.e., it closes the short circuit switch without the operator’s release. It was reported in previous publications of the authors that repetitive Damped Oscillatory Waves (DOW) cause malfunctioning of the time-phase controller. However, answering the question about the origin of the DOWs and the number of DOWs is elaborated only in this paper, using numerical simulation of the transients in the MV supply line. In the paper, a numerical model of the three-phase circuit is presented. Transients that follow closing of the MW CB are simulated. Numerical simulations confirm that the origin of DOWs is the closing of the MV CB, and the repetition of DOW is due to different instances of closing the switch in each phase.

articleTitle: Predicting the Electromagnetic Characteristics of an Unknown Antenna Using Noisy or Phaseless Sparse Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Identifying the electromagnetic characteristics and vulnerability of unknown antennas is crucial for efficient electronic warfare, electromagnetic attacks, and antenna system defense. To accurately predict the overall electromagnetic characteristics of an unknown antenna, it is imperative to gather and utilize various indicators obtained by aerial reconnaissance. Based on the acquired magnitude and phase data of the sparsely radiated electric field, the antenna can be modeled using a linear fitting algorithm on a uniform three-dimensional grid. However, in practical measurements of radiation patterns by aerial reconnaissance, significant noise generally contaminates the observed magnitude and phase data to render it ineffective. This results in typical scenarios wherein only magnitude data are observed owing to various environmental variables or system-related factors. Therefore, further research is required to determine the approach to performing infinitesimal dipole modeling (IDM) using incomplete data. This study analyzed the performance of IDM in the presence of noise-contaminated magnitude and phase. It proposes a method for performing IDM using a non-linear optimization algorithm only for magnitude information. The algorithm is based on the phaseless data of collected sparse radiation patterns. We employed a levenberg-marquardt algorithm for non-linear optimization. For both simulations and measurements, a rigid horn antenna with a center frequency of 2.4 GHz was utilized. It was observed that increasing the noise ratio in sparse data caused an increase in errors. Even in the worst-case scenario of phaseless data, the nonlinear optimization-based IDM demonstrated remarkable recognition performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Measurement Noise Effects in the Close Environment of Equivalent Near-Field Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Based on the surface equivalence principle an equivalent near-field source can be determined by measurements with a near-field scanner. One application is to use the source to simulate the interferences of the device-under-test with other objects in its close environment. Due to a limited signal-to-noise ratio in practical applications, noise adds to the near-field source. Hence, noise effects affect the quality of the simulation results and cause uncertainties. The influence of the noise effects is investigated by a simulative approach with artificially added noise. Two test devices with different a geometric dimension, operating frequency and excited power are evaluated for different characteristics and signal-to-noise ratios to assess the impact of the simulation results. Finally, in a combined simulation an equivalent near-field source will disturb an IoT-device and the voltages at two resistors on the device are examined.

articleTitle: IGBT’s Ageing and its Impacts on the EM Conducted Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: IGBTs play crucial roles in various power electronic applications, demanding reliability over extended periods. Understanding their failure mechanisms is vital for manufacturers and engineers. This study addresses gaps by correlating IGBT degradation, particularly die-attach and gate oxide contamination, with conducted electromagnetic (EM) disturbances. Accelerated ageing was conducted on 600V, 16A IGBTs using a power cycling system, revealing significant changes in static and dynamic parameters. Switching transients showed a slowdown in turn-off, attributed to the experienced degradation. Experimental setups demonstrated a direct link between degradation, switching transients, especially collector current (IC) turn-off, and reduced conducted EM disturbances.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of the Model of Traction Current Distribution in Rails to Variability in Impedances and Admittances of the Rail Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The traction network of electrified railways is a powerful spatially distributed source of electromagnetic interference over a wide frequency range, which affects the operation of railway signaling systems. The problem solved in this work is related to the sensitivity analysis of the model of the distribution of return traction current in the rails to the variability of their electrical parameters. The construction of a fairly complete and adequate model of the traction network is complicated by a number of factors, including its large length, differences in design and parameters in its different sections, nonlinearity of the electrical parameters of some of its elements, non-stationary processes in the traction network, which is caused by changes in the position and operating modes of the rolling stock, as well as a large number of wires of various types in the network, including rails that are electrically connected to the ground, which leads to variability in their parameters under the influence of external factors. Significant variability in rail parameters affects not only the uncertainty of modeling results, but also the possibility of model validation. The purpose of this work is to study the sensitivity of the differential return traction current distribution model in rails to the variability of rail impedance and rail-to-earth conductance. Sensitivity analysis of the model to the variability of its parameters allows us to determine the degree of its adequacy in relation to a specific task.

articleTitle: Multichannel EMI Filter Performance Assessment by Mix Mode Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Multichannel measurements allow faster evaluation of Insertion Loss (IL) for Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) filters than traditional methods. This paper presents the multichannel measurement technique which enables determining both Differential Mode (DM) and Common Mode (CM) IL. The presented technique requires only one setup instead of the multiple separate setups described in CISPR 17. Furthermore, the measurement speed is increased in the current approach, by a single injection of Mixed Mode to characterize an Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) filter in terms of DM and CM IL. Limitations of this method have been highlighted and described including, Dynamic Range (DNR) and mode interactions. Simulations and measurements have been performed to validate the proposed theory. It has been concluded that a single sweep measurement can be used for determining the IL of an EMI filter.

articleTitle: Influence of Electrode Surface Roughness on Electromagnetic Field Radiation Due to Micro-Gap ESD Below 1 kV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Impulsive transient electromagnetic fields caused by electrostatic discharge (ESD) have a serious influence on modern IT high-tech equipment. However, the mechanism and transient characteristics of electromagnetic noise radiation by ESD have not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, in order to elucidate the radiation mechanism of transient electromagnetic waves due to micro gap ESD at charging voltages below 800 V, the relationship between the surface roughness of electrode and the radiation field strength was investigated experimentally. As a result, it was found that the electrode surface roughness affects the radiated electric field strength due to ESD, and when the electrode surface roughness is 3 μm or less, the electromagnetic field strength increases by about 14 V/m. Furthermore, the correlation between the electrode surface roughness and the radiation field strength showed a negative correlation from 450V to 600V, and a positive correlation from 700 V to 800 V.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Correction Factors for In Situ H-Field Measurements below 2 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A large number of devices cannot be tested in standard electromagnetic compatibility laboratories due to size, power or safety-related constraints. In these cases, the only viable alternative is the in situ approach. The reference standard for in situ testing, CISPR 11, proposes to evaluate the equipment’s emissions in the 150 kHz to 30 MHz range through the measurement of the magnetic field at a 30 m distance. However, at such conditions, the said emissions are barely discernible from ambient noise and sometimes ensuring such fixed measuring distances is not even possible due to limitations of the test site. Emerging standards projects, e.g., CISPR 37, are considering setting the reference distance to 10 m while allowing measures at distances from 3 m to 30 m through the application of specific conversion factors to achieve a result that is comparable to the applicable disturbance limits. In this work, the corresponding magnetic field conversion factors are experimentally studied and validated from the in situ standpoint. Results obtained show an excellent match with the proposal in the latest CISPR 37 draft in the frequency range from 150 kHz to 2 MHz.

articleTitle: Effect of Corrosion on Electromagnetic Reliability for the High-Voltage Shield Cable of Electrification Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: High-voltage cables are the power transfer path between high-voltage components, but they are also the transmission path for electromagnetic noise. These cables are mounted on the exterior of the vehicle and are prone to corrosion. When high-voltage cables corrode, the electrical properties of the metal shielding layer change, which can affect the shielding performance of the cable. In this paper, we observe the changes in the electrical properties of the cable when the metal-braided shielding layer of the cable is corroded, and analyze the shielding performance of the cable based on international standards. In addition, the electromagnetic radiation emission test of high-voltage components with corroded cables is conducted to analyze the impact on electromagnetic noise emission. As a result, we experimentally verify the importance of electromagnetic reliability (EMR) of vehicle components through shielding systems such as high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conducted Emission with influences of operating frequencies and amplitudes of a selfoscillating capacitive touch sensing circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of human-machine interfaces (HMI), particularly in the realm of touch screen technologies, capacitive touch sensing has gained prominence due to its superior flexibility and cost-effectiveness compared to other touch interfaces, such as resistive-based methods, infrared touch sensors, and surface acoustic wave sensors. However, this advancement comes with increased emission and susceptibility to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) and similar disturbances, notably due to factors like operating sensing frequency and voltage. The previous research underscored the challenges of Electromagnetic Emission and some drawbacks of operating capacitive sensors at higher excitation frequencies. Characteristics of traditional capacitance to digital circuits like sigma-delta capacitive sensing circuits operate at higher frequencies, thus producing challenges in terms of emission and susceptibility. This paper offers a detailed assessment of the conducted electromagnetic emissions in a self-oscillating capacitance-to-time converter. The study primarily investigates how conducted emission characteristics change in response to the sensing circuit’s operating frequency and voltage variations. The oscillating capacitive sensing circuit conducts sensing with a single clock cycle, thus mitigating some of the issues associated with the traditional capacitive sensing circuits, such as sigma-delta capacitive sensing, which generally require a higher frequency of operations. The results indicate that as the sensing frequency and the operating voltage decrease, the conducted emission of the sensor improves; this phenomenon can be particularly beneficial in high EMI environments like the automotive industry, where capacitive touch sensors are placed close to sensitive electronics.

articleTitle: Behavioral Model of Inductors via Physics-Informed Circuit Synthesis and Modified Vector Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed circuit synthesis method to obtain behavioral models of inductors, the parameters of which are determined by a modified vector fitting (MVF) routine. Although the vector fitting (VF) algorithm provides accurate numerical approximation of virtually any frequency response in form of poles and residues, the most common circuit synthesis methods often lead to unphysical electrical parameters (e.g. negative resistances), which correctly fit frequency responses, but cannot be used in common time-domain simulators such as Matlab Simulink. On the contrary, the methodology here proposed specifically for inductors produces circuit models with physical, easily interpretable circuit elements, such as the low-frequency functional inductance, the winding capacitance responsible for self-resonance frequency (SRF), and additional physical components to correctly fit multiple resonances. The proposed method is experimentally compared with a straightforward equation-based method and the original VF method in terms of accuracy, simplicity, and compatibility with common, commercial circuit solvers.

articleTitle: Numerical Computation of In-cell Parameters for Multiwire Formalism in FDTD
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain method is a very suitable tool to analyse the propagation of, among others, lightning and arcing through new high voltage high power distribution networks in aircraft. This paper presents a numerical method for the computation of the in-cell inductance and in-cell capacitance matrices, required to accurately model wire bundles in a finite-difference time-domain grid. The method extends the multiwire formalism proposed by Bérenger, and enables the inclusion of inhomogeneous media, as well as non-cylindrical conductors. Moreover, the method accurately computes the interactions between closely spaced wires that are neglected by the analytical formulation of Bérenger. The presented method is applied to a testcase that can be compared to Bérenger’s results. Finally, results for a testcase that involves dielectric insulation are given.

articleTitle: Improved Determination of the Electric Field in Radiated IEMI Tests with EMP and UWB Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The reproduction, amplification and measurement of representative intentional electromagnetic interference waveforms in a GTEM cell is presented without the necessity of access to dedicated electromagnetic pulse generators. Moreover, practical guidance on the transfer function characterization of a GTEM cell for high-voltage arbitrary transient tests is provided.

articleTitle: Models for Evaluating the Shielding Properties of Products Made of Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A model for evaluating the shielding properties of products (conductive gaskets, shields, absorbing panels, etc.) made of composites is developed. The model allows to calculate the shielding effectiveness of EMI gaskets and flat absorbing panels. Initial data are geometrical parameters of products and general information about the internal structure of the composite material. The validity of the model is confirmed by comparison with the results of experiments in the frequency range from 800 MHz to 16 GHz.

articleTitle: Conducted Emissions of an upto 2.3 kW Interleaved SiC Buck Converter under Varied Operative Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Wide band gap semiconductors such as siliconcarbide (SiC)-based devices are favored in the power electronic industry for their reduced switching losses. However, their utilization leads to high $\mathrm{d} V_{\mathrm{DS}} / \mathrm{d} t$, causing high-frequency emissions that can affect the operation of connected devices and systems on the board net. This study investigates conducted emissions originating from the output lines of a laboratory adaptation of an automotive interleaved buck converter, interfacing the traction battery of an electric vehicle with 48 V board net, along with monitoring the chip temperature of the SiC MOSFET. Across various combinations of input and output characteristics and operation modes, differences in common and differential mode emission spectra and their comparison with CISPR-25 standard limits, are observed. A study is further done to analyze these experimental results.

articleTitle: Software-Defined Radio Techniques for Enhanced OFDM Transmission in NVIS Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This study presents the development of a data communication system that operates in the high frequency (HF) frequency range using the Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM) modulation technique. The system consists of a transmitter and receiver built on Software-Defined Radio (SDR) platforms and uses the GNU Radio software framework. The NVIS (Near Vertical Incidence Skywave) communication system has been designed and tested under both laboratory and real field conditions over a link distance of 180 kilometers. The laboratory tests evaluated the performance of OFDM modulation, considering factors such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), packet error rate (PER), packet length, number of subcarriers, and bandwidths ranging from 3 kHz to 24 kHz.

articleTitle: Comparison of FIR Filter Lengths and Adaptation Methods in Digital Active EMI Filters based on Delay-Compensated Digital Gate Control Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Modern motor inverters use steep switching waveforms to reduce losses and high switching frequencies for a high power density. This makes inverters potential sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI), which is usually reduced by large and heavy passive EMI filters. The idea of Active EMI Filters (AEF) is to reduce size and weight of the passive filter circuit. Digital Active EMI Filters (DAEF) based on FIR (finite impulse response) filter structures can achieve very high performance when used in feed-forward mode with an estimated, predicted anti-noise signal. Hereby, the anti-noise signal is calculated by a FIR filter, whose input signal is the superposition of the digital gate control signals. The time required to calculate and inject the anti-noise signal is compensated by adding a short delay to the digital gate control signals before arriving at the gate driver. In this work, a comparison of different FIR filter lengths and adaptation methods for Common Mode (CM) EMI reduction in a motor drive system is presented. A further development of the delayed digital control (DDC)-DAEF implementation is introduced, in which the filter weights are calculated iteratively using the Wiener-Hopfequation. Results are presented and discussed for a freewheeling and a mechanically loaded inverter-motor system.

articleTitle: Assessing the Response Time of a Frequency-Selective EMD Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Traditionally, the measurement of electromagnetic disturbances (EMDs) relies on field probes equipped with diode or thermocouple detectors. Some of those detectors may not adept at capturing rapidly changing electromagnetic (EM) fields, and may be plagued by slow response times that can lead to erroneous measurements. Furthermore, those detectors operate in the time domain, producing broadband EM field strength results without the ability to identify specific frequencies where EMDs occur. This paper introduces the design and assessment of a frequency-selective EMD detector using software-defined radios (SDRs). The proposed system detects and transforms undesired EMD signals from the time domain to the frequency domain via an embedded Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). When the electric field strength exceeds a predefined threshold within the SDR-based detector, it triggers a warning. To measure the speed of the SDR-based detector response to an EMD, pulse-modulated signals were selected as the test signals. The frequency hopping time is also considered a crucial element affecting the SDR-based detector response time. The experimental results for response time are subsequently subjected to a Monte Carlo-based simulation, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the SDR-based detector response time.

articleTitle: On RadCom channel capacity for V2V applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The use of Millimiter Wave (mmWave) for communication and sensing purposes is one of the functions powered by Next Generation Vehicle-to-Anything (V2X) networks. The arrival of IEEE 802.11bd, which is able to operate in the 60 GHz band, opens the doors of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) to vehicular networks. Similarly, Radar-based Communication (RadCom) proposes the use of the radar spectrum for communication puproses. In this paper, we perform an analysis of the channel capacity for different configurations of RadCom, showing its potential to offload the V2X spectrum for bumper-to-bumper V2X applications. We finalize with a discussion on the potential for ISAC from both the 802.11bd and RadCom approaches.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Pixelated Antennas Regarding Pixel Size and Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Pixelated structures offer a unique possibility to design and optimize antennas tailor-made for very specific and challenging application scenarios, where conventional antenna design may lead to unsatisfactory results. Several different optimization techniques can be applied to these structures, depending on the desired goals and applications, making pixelated antennas very versatile fundamental structures. In this study, we investigate the optimization of pixelated antennas with a focus on the effects of pixel size and asymmetrical design approaches on gain. By simulation techniques and optimization algorithms, including genetic algorithms and multi-objective frameworks, we analyze how these design parameters influence the antenna’s performance in terms of gain. Our findings reveal that smaller pixel sizes enhance the gain of large antennas, while asymmetrical designs offer advantages over symmetrical configurations.

articleTitle: Data-Efficient Prediction of the Specific Absorption Rate in a Human Head Model Exposed to a Plane EM Wave Using Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this contribution, the specific absorption rate (SAR) in a human head model exposed to a 13.56 MHz external electromagnetic (EM) wave is predicted using Gaussian process regression (GPR). The electrical properties of the tissues are varied around the nominal values by $\pm 20 \%$ to account for material uncertainties. The GPR model achieves an $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ regression score higher than 0.99. The maximum and the worst-case exposure over the variation space are found using a tenth of the samples needed by random sampling on average. This allows the fast comparison against standards with a high degree of confidence. A sensitivity analysis of the exposure is extracted from the GPR model to provide an insight into the effects of the different parameter variations. The proposed framework is applicable to radiated susceptibility scenarios and beyond.

articleTitle: Investigation of Frequency-Dependent Electrical Properties of Nanocomposites Based on Epoxy Resin Reinforced with Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A comprehensive investigation is conducted to characterize nanocomposite systems composed of an epoxy resin and different concentrations (0.3,0.5,1,1.5,2 and $3 \mathbf{w t} \%$) of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). The study focuses on assessing their electromagnetic properties over a frequency range spanning from 100Hz to 1MHz. Complex impedance, dielectric constant, and conductivity are systematically examined, and the results are consistently correlated with theoretical aspects. Understanding the intricate frequency-dependent electrical dynamics of nanocomposites is crucial to optimize their performances and to further promote the next-generation of polymer-based technologies.

articleTitle: On Sensitivity Analysis Techniques for PE Circuit Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: One of the problems in the Power Electronic (PE) circuit design is the incorporation of parasitic elements in the design and simulation stage. Sensitivity Analysis (SA) allows to identify the parameters that have the highest influence on the variation of the output, thus allowing to efficiently target Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) mitigation techniques. In this paper results of applying several sensitivity analysis methods to a PE circuit are juxtaposed and it is shown how identifying the parameters can help in reducing the Common Mode (CM) current of the PE under consideration.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Approach to Defining Emission Limits in Terms of Total Radiated Power
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A method of defining emission limits in terms of total radiated disturbance power is presented, which is effective for testing mobile and portable devices. The radiated power from equipment under test can be measured in a reverberation chamber (RC), which is an attractive alternative to a fully anechoic room (FAR) because of its space factor, cost effectiveness, and higher measurement sensitivity. Usually, the radiated power measured in RC is converted to the maximum field strength and compared with the relevant limit in tests in FAR. This conversion needs an assumption on the unknown maximum directivity of disturbance radiation, which is a major cause of uncertainty. The approach presented here enables us to derive a radiated power limit without knowing the maximum directivity of radiation. Disturbance radiation with high directivity generally increases the maximum field strength at the radio receiver being interfered, but at the same time, it decreases the probability that the maximum directivity is in the direction of the receiver. The limit derivation is based on the principle that the effects of the above two factors on the probability of interference cancel each other when the source device meets certain conditions.

articleTitle: Reciprocal Influence of Supply and Demand Quality in Remote Off-grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The provision of electricity to the most remote areas is part of Sustainable Development Goal 7, which aims for universal energy access. This can be assessed partially through the Multi-Tier Framework attributes. The quality of electricity is one of the attributes that is often overlooked, despite its significance to the system’s electromagnetic compatibility. This oversight can be attributed to the challenging circumstances in remote areas, characterized by limited resources and infrastructure. Aiming to emphasize the importance of quality attributes, this study investigates how harmonics manifests in the system with an emphasis on the reciprocal influence of the supply and demand quality. A specific context of the remote off-grid system was modelled as a converter-based generation supplying electricity to a cluster of households. The simulation results indicate that the presence of nonlinear loads in the system could induce harmonics throughout the system and ensuring good supply quality does not guarantee immunity to harmonics induced by the nonlinear loads. Consequently, it is imperative to ensure both supply and demand qualities are sufficiently robust to comply with harmonic standards.

articleTitle: Application of an AI-assisted Approach for Efficient EMI Source Characterization based on the Spherical Wave Expansion Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Accurate estimation of unwanted electromagnetic radiation is becoming nowadays a hot topic for a large set of cutting-edge electronic devices and applications, like for instance high-performance computing systems and server units. The possibility to reconstruct the radiation from a source is a fundamental feature for modern system designers, capable of paving the way also to the possibility of estimating the overall radiation coming from a set of radiation sources, like stacks of server units in a data center. However, most of the time, the radiation source can be characterized (measured) only in terms of the amplitude of the radiated field and this fact prevents the possibility of accurately predicting the overall radiation from several sources. This work aims to present an approach based on Machine Learning techniques and suitable to efficiently characterize a radiation source in terms of its Spherical Wave Coefficients only by using field amplitude data as input. Since the scope of the work is to present the mere proof-of-concept, well-established Neural Network-based Machine Learning algorithms will be used in the proposed method. The general framework and some simulation analyses to validate the method are proposed.

articleTitle: EM Risk Management for Wireless Communications: First Look and Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: With the increased application of wireless communication in mission and safety-critical applications, such as autonomous vehicles, concerns have been raised regarding the reliability and safety of these technologies. Especially of interest is the dependability of these technologies under Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). In the field of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC), the idea of Electromagnetic Risk Management (EMRM) forms a promising way of tackling dependability related issues stemming from EMI. In the field of wireless communications, research for mission and safety-critical applications have resulted in Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) technologies. This paper draws parallels between EMRM and URLLC and provides a view on EMRM for wireless communications, which aims to make URLLC systems dependable under EMI. To support the idea of EMRM for wireless communications, a small case study is provided which shows the vulnerability of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) frame synchronization to Narrowband Interference (NBI) and indicates a necessity for research into EMRM for wireless communications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for the Geolocalization of Jamming Sources in Indoor Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Jamming attacks produce malicious interference on wireless communication systems. The early and accurate localization of a jammer is extremely important in critical indoor environments, like airports and operating rooms. We employ electromagnetic simulations based on the ray tracing technique for quickly creating a dataset mapping the effects of the jammer on passive antennas in an indoor environment. Our simulation methodology is experimentally validated in a real scenario, using a commercial jammer and a multiport software defined radio transceiver. This dataset is further exploited using machine learning approaches to obtain an accurate localization of a jammer. The limitations of the proposed approach are also explored according to the measurement noise.

articleTitle: Advanced Numerical High-Fidelity Real-Time Dosimetry Simulations of Low-Frequency Magnetic Fields for Inductive Charging of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Inductive charging of electric vehicles as a method of wireless energy transfer involves low-frequency magnetic fields to which people inside or in the vicinity of the vehicles are exposed. The magnetic field and related electric field intensities induced in the human body are subject to restrictions established by the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection to avoid possible harmful biological effects. As part of an environmental electromagnetic compatibility analysis, numerical simulations of these exposure scenarios involve high-resolution voxel body phantoms. Within the Co-Simulation Scalar Potential Finite-Difference scheme, these numerical simulations repeatedly solve linear discrete Poisson systems in the range of nearly ten million degrees of freedom. Combining the underlying two-step approach with on-site magnetic field measurements modifies this scheme into a measurement-based variant, which requires solving these linear algebraic systems in real-time. Near-real-time solution techniques are presented involving highly parallelized algebraic multigrid-based solvers running on expensive multiple Graphics Processing Units-accelerated hardware and recently developed highly efficient reduced-order model formulations running on low-cost computing devices such as e.g., Raspberry Pi.

articleTitle: AI-tailored Slew-rate Gate Drive Scheme for Low Emission Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The growth of Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs) in the automotive landscape has propelled the need for high efficiency and increased payload for the vehicle design. This leads to systems and components being packed in the immediate vicinity of each other, disregarding the coupling through the voltage or frequency content. Thus, an innovative approach to balance the demands of increased propulsion system efficiency enabling long driving range with an Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) oversight is indispensable.
